5. After the 2nd Prokimenon – immediately "Vouchsafe"

6. **Aposticha:** Aposticha of the *Triodion*

7. After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" – Troparion to the Saint, Glory, Both now: Dismissal Theotokion of the tone and of the day of the week[^500]. (On Friday evening – Theotokion from the Sunday ones in the tone of the Troparion)

8. Litany "Have mercy on us, O God" and 3 great prostrations, without prayer

9. "O All-holy Trinity", "Blessed be the name of the Lord", "I will bless the Lord", *“It is truly meet”* and dismissal from "Glory to Thee, O Christ God".

> **Note:** Although according to the rubric on Wednesday and Friday the Liturgy is not celebrated, nor the Presanctified, nevertheless, the Synod of Lviv permits our churches to celebrate also on these days the Liturgy of Chrysostom[^501].

##### At Compline

On Wednesday evening we read Small [Compline]. We do not take the Canon of the Theotokos[^502], but we sing the Canon of the *Menaion* of the saint who falls on Saturday.

#### On Cheesefare Thursday

##### At Matins

, AT THE HOURS AND AT THE LITURGY

Everything – according to the general rule for a saint without Polyeleos on weekdays, however, at Matins look for the rubric here on page 324.

#### On Cheesefare Friday

On Cheesefare Thursday evening and on Friday morning we sing the service exactly as on Wednesday, here on [pp. 324-325](#on-cheesefare-wednesday-and-friday).

#### On Cheesefare Saturday

We commemorate all the Venerable Fathers who shone forth in asceticism.

##### At Vespers

On Friday evening everything – according to the rubric for Wednesday evening, here on page 322.

##### At Compline

1. Instead of the Theotokion Canon we sing the Canon for the Dead of the *Octoechos* of the current tone from Matins

2. After *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion of the Fathers[^503]

##### At Matins

1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Troparion of the Fathers twice, Glory, Both now: Sunday Theotokion in the tone of the Troparion of the Fathers

2. Two Kathismata with Sessional Hymns of the *Triodion*, Psalm 50 immediately Canon

3. **Canons:** Canons 2 on 14: of the Temple Saint with heirmos on 6 and of the *Triodion* of the Fathers on 8. Katavasia – Heirmos of the Canon of the Fathers. We read the usual refrains. (To the Canon of the Fathers – "Venerable Fathers, pray to God for us")[^504]

After the 3rd Ode – Sessional Hymn of the Fathers; after the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos of the Fathers, after the 9th – Exaposteilarion of the Fathers.

4. 4 Stichera of the Praises of the Fathers, Glory: of the Fathers, Both now: Theotokion

5. **After the Great Doxology:** Troparion to the Fathers, Glory, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones in the tone of the [Troparion of] the Fathers

6. **Dismissal:** Great Dismissal with commemoration of the Fathers

##### At the Hours

At all – Troparion and Kontakion of the Fathers.

##### At the Divine Liturgy

Everything – only to the Fathers, and the Epistle and Gospel first of the day, and then – to the Fathers.

### 4.1.6 Cheesefare Sunday

Of the Expulsion of Adam

We sing everything according to the rubric of the Sunday of the Prodigal Son, here on page 319.

#### On Cheesefare Sunday And On All Sundays Of Great Lent

##### At Vespers

> **Notes** 

1. Since the five first weekdays of each week of Great Lent, that is Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday have a service of Lenten form, beginning from Sunday evening, we use sacred vestments of Lenten colors, according to the previous rubric – purple, according to the Synod of Lviv – violet

2. We do not make prostrations at Vespers of these Sundays from the beginning of Vespers, but from "Vouchsafe, O Lord". We make, therefore, three small prostrations after "Vouchsafe, O Lord" and at the Trisagion following "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart"; and 3 great prostrations – at the troparia, at "Virgin Theotokos" and at the prayer of St. Ephrem, without the 12 small ones[^505]

3. No Kathisma

4. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: 4 Penitential of the *Octoechos* of the current tone, 2 given at the Aposticha of Vespers and 2 at the Aposticha of Matins (which are taken from the *Octoechos* and given at the end of the *Triodion*), 3 of the *Triodion* and 3 of the *Menaion* of the saint; Glory: of the saint, Both now: Usual Theotokion in the tone of the Doxastikon; if none, then Glory, Both now: Theotokion from the *Menaion*

- If two saints fall, we sing to one in the evening 3 stichera, and to the other the Stichera of the Praises on 4[^506].

- If a saint on 6 falls, we sing to him 3 stichera, just as to a saint on 4[^507].

5. **Entrance:** Entrance, on account of the Great Prokimenon

6. Instead of the Prokimenon of the day we sing the Great Prokimenon of the *Triodion* (on this Sunday, on the 2nd and 4th: "Turn not away"; on the 1st, 3rd and 5th: "Thou Hast given an inheritance")

7. After the Prokimenon there will be no litany[^508]; the Priest takes off the phelonion and closes the holy doors, and we say "Vouchsafe, O Lord" and after this we make 3 small prostrations

8. **Aposticha:** Aposticha of the *Triodion* with the usual verses of the *Horologion*, only, if there be Glory: of the saint, then the Theotokion will be the usual one, in the tone of the Doxastikon

9. After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" and the Trisagion with three small prostrations we sing 3 troparia with prostrations, that is "Virgin Theotokos" and a prostration, Glory: "O Baptizer of Christ" and a prostration; Both now: "Intercede for us" and a prostration, and then "Beneath Thy tender mercy" without a prostration

10. "Lord, have mercy" (40) and the rest, as in the *Horologion*, however, only up to the end of the 3rd great prostration of the prayer of St. Ephrem, we do not make other small prostrations[^509], but the Priest immediately: "Glory to Thee, O Christ God" and the dismissal of the day with the commemoration of the saint.

##### At Compline

We sing Small Compline with the Lenten prostrations, that is 3 small prostrations at "Glory to God in the highest", at the Trisagion following *“It is truly meet”* and after the prayer of St. Ephrem[^510] and 16 usual ones at the prayer of St. Ephrem. We do not omit the Canon of the Theotokos, since there was no All-Night Vigil.

### 4.1.7 Beginning of Great Lent

> **Note:** The Synod of Lviv permits on all days of Great Lent, except Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, meat, on the condition of [reciting] 5 "Our Father" and 5 "Virgin Theotokos" for the laity, and Psalm 50 – for the clergy; on the other three days – dairy products.

GENERAL RUBRICS

FOR THE FIVE FIRST LENTEN DAYS OF ALL WEEKS

OF GREAT LENT

##### At the Midnight Office

On the first day of Great Lent we do not make prostrations at the Midnight Office, except three great ones at the prayer of St. Ephrem, and on other Lenten days we make 3 small prostrations: 1. At each of the three Trisagions. 2. At both "O come, let us worship". 3. At each Glory: "The Blameless"; also 16 usual ones at the prayer of St. Ephrem, that is 4 great and 12 small[^511].

##### At Matins

> **Note:** We begin prostrations from the Kathismata and make: 1. At "Alleluia" of each "Glory" of the Kathismata – 3 prostrations[^512]. 2. At "More honorable" of each of the 6 verses of the Song of the Theotokos – 1 prostration. 3. At *“It is truly meet”* – 1 prostration. 4. At "Glory to God in the highest" – 3 prostrations. 5. At the final Trisagion – 3 prostrations. 6. At the prayer of St. Ephrem – 16 prostrations, that is 12 small and 4 great.

1. From the beginning to the end of the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord", everything, just as on every day

2. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Instead of *“God is the Lord”* we sing Alleluia in the sequential tone of the *Octoechos*

3. We sing three Trinity Hymns of the current tone, given in the *Horologion*, three for each tone. They are all sung three times with the refrain "Glory" to the second, and "Both now" – to the third. At each first one we make a commemoration of the weekday service, at the second – a commemoration of all saints, at the third – a commemoration of the Theotokos. However, since the weekday service of the week changes daily, and the troparia are sung the same each day of the week (except Saturdays and Sundays, on which, because they are not Lenten, the Trinity Hymns are not sung), at the end of each first Trinity Hymn a colon is given, which signifies that the troparion must be completed with the commemoration of the weekday service, the form of which is indicated at the end of the 3rd troparion of Tone 1

Note

These three commemorations we make also at the Exaposteilaria following the canon. But the Lenten Exaposteilarion has only one troparion in each tone, which is sung three times, therefore, when it is sung the first time, the commemoration of the weekday service is added to it, when – the second time, with the refrain "Glory", then – the commemoration of all saints, and when the third time, with the refrain "Both now", then – the commemoration of the Theotokos. These commemorations are added where the colon is given, that is before "And save me".

4. Three Kathismata with their Sessional Hymns, the Sessional Hymns of which, sung after the 1st Kathisma, are of the *Octoechos* of the current tone, given also at the end of the *Triodion*. The Sessional Hymns sung after the 2nd and 3rd Kathismata are of the *Triodion*

5. Psalm 50 and the first petition of the Great Litany "Save, O God", and after the exclamation "Through the mercy and compassion" immediately – the Canon

6. Odes and Canons. The Biblical Odes, given at the end of the Psalter, are intertwined with the odes of the canon, as given: before the ode of the canon the corresponding ode of the Psalter is recited, leaving its last verses for refrains to the troparia of the canon, in such quantity as there will be troparia in the ode of the canon, including the heirmos, except two, for to the penultimate troparion we refrain "Glory", and to the last – "Both now". The 2nd Ode is recited in full before the ode of the canon, and to the troparia of its canon we refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee". According to our ancient custom, the Odes of the Psalter are recited only in those odes in which the triodion occurs, and in the other odes we refrain the usual refrains to the troparia of the canon. The Greek Typikon prescribes singing the Odes of the Psalter in the tone of the *Menaion* canon, but now we do not even know what their melody was

The Canons will be only of the *Menaion* and *Triodion*, for the *Octoechos*, according to the Greek rubric, during Great Lent is not sung, with the exception of Sundays. In some odes there will be 3 canons on 14, that is of the Saint of the *Menaion* with heirmos on 6 and both canons of the *Triodion* on 8: one on 4 and the second on 4. In some odes there will be only one canon of the saint on 4, and in the second ode there will be only two canons of the *Triodion* on 8, with heirmos on 9. This difference regarding the number of canons and their troparia in the odes arises because the *Triodion* canons do not occur daily in all odes, but in general only in three odes in the following sequence:

#### On Monday: 1St, 8Th And 9Th.

#### On Tuesday: 2Nd, 8Th And 9Th.

#### On Wednesday: 3Rd, 8Th And 9Th.

#### On Thursday: 4Th, 8Th And 9Th.

#### On Friday: 5Th, 8Th And 9Th.

#### On Saturday: 6Th, 7Th, 8Th And 9Th.

Therefore, there will be:

On Monday: at Odes 1, 8, and 9 – 3 canons on 14, that is of the *Menaion* with heirmos on 6 and both canons of the triodion on 8, and afterwards – one more separate troparion of the *Triodion* with the refrain "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", and the Katavasia – Heirmos of the 2nd canon of the triodion. At other odes there will be only one canon of the saint on 4, with heirmos on 5; only at Odes 3 and 6 the canon of the saint is read without the heirmos, for it is taken afterwards, as Katavasia[^513].

On Tuesday: at the 2nd Ode, since the saint does not have this ode, there will be only two canons of the triodion on 8, and afterwards – one more separate troparion and Katavasia – Heirmos of the 2nd canon of the triodion; at the 8th and 9th Odes – 3 canons on 14 exactly as on Monday. At other odes there will be only the canon of the *Menaion* on 4 exactly as on Monday.

On Wednesday: at the 3rd, 8th, and 9th Odes there will be 3 canons on 14 exactly as at the 1st, 8th, and 9th Odes on Monday. And at other odes there will be only one canon of the saint on 4, as on Monday.

On Thursday: at the 4th, 8th, and 9th Odes there will be 3 canons on 14, as on Monday. At other odes – only the canon of the saint on 4 and the rest, as on Monday.

On Friday: at the 5th, 8th, and 9th Odes there will be 3 canons on 14, as on Monday; and at other odes – only one of the saint on 4.

On Saturday: at the 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th Odes there will be 3 canons: one of the saint and two of the *Triodion*, at other odes there will be two canons: of the temple and of the saint; however, for Saturday a separate rubric will be given, since Saturday is not a Lenten day.

• If two saints fall, then we read both their canons together on 6[^514], that is of the first saint with heirmos on 3 and of the second without heirmos on 3. So also to the saint on 6.

The Katavasia will be always the heirmos of the last canon either of the triodion, or of the *Menaion*: of the triodion where there will be a triodion, and where there will be only the *Menaion*, then the Katavasia of the *Menaion* will be only after Odes 3 and 6, for at the 8th and 9th there will always be a triodion and therefore there will always be the Katavasia of the triodion.

A more precise example of the combination of the Odes of the Psalter with the Odes of the Canon is given at the 1st Ode in the Moscow Typikon, and is presented as follows: "After this we begin: 'Let us sing to the Lord' in the tone of the canon of the *Menaion* of the saint of the day and the verses of the odes are recited hurriedly, each Choir – its verse, until they reach 'The waters became thick' and from this they begin verses on 14, and we sing the *Menaion* with heirmos on 6. And we sing thus: the first Choir reads the verse 'The waters became thick' and sings the heirmos. The second Choir reads the second verse 'The enemy said' and, after it, – the troparion of the canon, and in sequence verses by choirs up to 'Then hastened'. From the verse 'Then hastened' we begin the triodion of Kyr Joseph on 4. And at 'The Lord reigning' we sing the 2nd triodion of Kyr Theodore the Studite, and one choir sings the troparion, and the second choir – the 2nd verse and the troparion. After this both choirs, having united, sing: Glory: Trinity Hymn, in a higher voice, Both now: Theotokion. Then we sing in the highest voice: 'Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee', and we sing the other troparion of Theodore, because the ode has 5 troparia. At the end we sing the Katavasia – heirmos of the second canon"[^515].

Regarding the refrains to the troparia of the canon, know that in order to find the number of refrains as quickly as possible, the last four, six, and eight verses of the Biblical Odes (except the 2nd, for it is read in full before the heirmos) from the bottom up are marked in the middle of the song, or on the side, with the inscription: "on 4, on 6, on 8". But on 14 they are not counted off, since 6 verses from 8 upwards are easily counted. However, the counting of 14 verses in current Psalters does not coincide exactly with the counting in previous Psalters, for where the rubrics place the 14th verse at "The waters became thick", current Psalters place the 14th verse at "The enemy said", and "The waters became thick" moves to the 15th verse. The 6th Ode has only 12 verses, so do not forget to divide these two verses of it on 4. The 9th Ode, one, of the Theotokos, is sung whole before the heirmos with "More honorable", and the other, of Zachariah, is sung whole in the refrains, and in those editions where there are only 13 verses, one verse must be divided into 2.

The last edition of the Lviv Psalter does not give the counting of the last verses, except for the 9th Ode; and, in general, in recent editions they did not care about the counting of verses.

After the 3rd Ode – Sessional Hymn of the Saint, after the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint; if the saint does not have this, then the Martyric Sessional Hymn of the *Octoechos* of the current tone[^516], given also at the end of the *Triodion*. After the 9th Ode – *“It is truly meet”* and after the litany – Exaposteilarion of the tone, which is in the *Horologion*, three times, with refrains and commemorations, as the Trinity Hymns, here on page 338, in the note.

7. **After the Great Doxology:** Before the Small Doxology the Priest exclaims: "To Thee belongs glory" and the rest, and at "Glory to God in the highest" we make three prostrations

8. **Aposticha:** Aposticha of the *Triodion*, Glory: of the saint, if there be, Both now: Usual Theotokion in the tone of "Glory"

3. "It is a good thing" twice; at the Trisagion – 3 prostrations and, after "Our Father", – Troparion "Standing in the temple"; then "Lord, have mercy" (40) and the rest with 16 prostrations at the prayer of St. Ephrem and, after the last prostration, immediately – "O come, let us worship" three times and the 1st Hour.

##### At the Hours

1. We make 3 small prostrations: at "O come, let us worship", at each Trisagion, at "Alleluia", which is after the three psalms, and at "Alleluia" after each antiphon; at each of the three singings of the troparion with two verses we bend the knees[^517] and, after the Theotokion, – 3 prostrations, and at the prayer of St. Ephrem – 16 usual ones

2. After the three psalms with "Alleluia" – Kathisma proper according to the Lenten marker of the Psalter, except the 1st Hour on Monday and the 1st and 9th Hours on Friday, for then there will be no Kathisma

3. **Troparia:** Troparion ("In the morning" at the 1st Hour, and at the others – the other one specific to the Hour) with two verses and with the bending of knees at each of the three singings of the troparion, then Glory, Both now: Theotokion ("What shall we call Thee" at the 1st, and at the others – the other, specific to the Hour)

4. Selected verses from the Holy Scripture of the Old Testament, that is: at the 1st Hour – "Direct my steps", at the 3rd – "Blessed is the Lord God", at the 6th Hour – "Let Thy compassions come quickly", at the 9th – "Forsake us not". At the 1st Hour "Direct my steps" is divided into 4 verses, of which we sing the first 3 twice, and the 4th – three times. At the 6th Hour between the Theotokion and the Old Testament verses we sing the Troparion of the Prophecy of the *Triodion* and one prophecy between two Prokimena there

5. After the Trisagion, instead of the Kontakion, we read three Lenten troparia, according to the order of the Hours in the *Horologion*, adding to the 2nd "Glory", and to the 3rd – "Both now"

6. "Lord, have mercy" (40), "Thou Who at all times" and the rest with the prostrations.

7. Trisagion with 3 prostrations, and after "Our Father" – the exclamation "For Thine is the Kingdom" and "Lord, have mercy" (12)

8. Final prayer of the Hour and "Glory to Thee, O Christ God", dismissal of the 1st Hour (or of the other Hours – their proper ones)

> **Notes** 

1. In the archcathedral temple the Hours 3rd, 6th, 9th, Typika and Vespers are celebrated together, beginning at 11 o'clock in the morning, and in the afternoon, at the usual time of Vespers, – Great Compline[^518].

2. The last prayer of the 9th Hour "O Master Lord Jesus Christ" is transferred to the Typika, to the place of the prayer "O All-holy Trinity", and the prayer "O All-holy Trinity" with the psalm following it is transferred, according to the rubric of our Pochaiv Triodion, to the end of Vespers[^519]. And on Wednesday and Friday, since Vespers will be with the Presanctified, "O All-holy Trinity" cannot be transferred to the end of Vespers, for it ends with the Liturgy and therefore remains in its place at the Typika, exactly so the prayer "O Master Lord Jesus Christ" remains in its place at the 9th Hour.

AT THE TYPIKA (Typika)

> **Note:** The first part of the Typika, from the beginning to the Beatitudes, falls out in Great Lent, and the last, from "O All-holy Trinity", is transferred to the end of Vespers. In the middle part the stichera on the Beatitudes and the Epistle and Gospel fall out.

1. "The Beatitudes", that is "Remember us, O Lord", "Blessed are the poor in spirit" and all other verses, then "Glory, Both now". After this both choirs, having come together, with uncovered heads, sing in a higher voice:

"Remember us, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom".

And a great prostration[^520].

"Remember us, O Master, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom".

And a great prostration.

"Remember us, O Holy One, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom".

And a great prostration.

2. "The Choir", verse and again "The Choir", Glory: "The Choir of holy angels", Both now: "I believe".

3. "Remit, pardon" and "Our Father".

10. Kontakia, which are in the *Horologion*

5. "Lord, have mercy" (40), "Glory, Both now" and the rest with the prayer of St. Ephrem and 16 usual prostrations, as in the *Horologion*.

11. Trisagion with 3 prostrations and the rest with "Our Father" and "Lord, have mercy" (12)

12. Priest – prayer of the 9th Hour "O Master Lord Jesus Christ"

13. **Dismissal:** Dismissal of the day with the commemoration of the saint[^521].

##### At Vespers

#### On Monday, Tuesday And Thursday Evening,

without Presanctified.

> **Note ** on Prostrations

We make three small prostrations: at "O come, let us worship", at "Alleluia" after the pre-introductory psalm and after each of the three antiphons of the Kathisma (although now we read only the beginning of the Kathisma); after "Vouchsafe, O Lord", at the Trisagions; at the prayer of St. Ephrem – 16 usual ones and one prostration after *“It is truly meet”*[^522].

Priest: "Blessed is our God"; choir: "O come, let us worship" three times with prostrations

After the pre-introductory psalm, at Alleluia, – 3 prostrations

3. 18th Kathisma with 3 prostrations at Alleluia after each of its antiphons (today we read only the beginning of the Kathisma).

1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 6 stichera: 3 of the *Triodion* and 3 of the *Menaion*, Glory, Both now: Theotokion of the *Menaion*. If there is a Doxastikon of the saint, then Theotokion – usual, in the tone of the Doxastikon

- If two saints fall, we sing to one in the evening stichera on 3, and to the 2nd in the morning at the Praises – stichera on 4[^523].

- If a saint on 6 falls, we sing to him stichera on 3, just as to a saint on 4; thus we sing also in the middle of a feast, e. g. December 20 and September 15.

Prokimenon of the *Triodion* and one reading of the *Triodion*, and afterwards also another Prokimenon and second reading of the *Triodion*

After the 2nd reading immediately – "Vouchsafe" and 3 prostrations

2. **Aposticha:** Aposticha of the *Triodion* with the usual verses of the *Horologion*. If there is a Doxastikon of the saint, then we select the Theotokion in His tone, as on *“Lord, I have cried”*; if not, then Glory, Both now: *Triodion*

After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", at the Trisagion, – 3 prostrations; and after "Our Father" – troparia "Virgin Theotokos" and the two others with a prostration at the end of each, then "Beneath Thy tender mercy" without a prostration

9. "Lord, have mercy" (40) and the rest, as in the *Horologion*, with the prayer of St. Ephrem and 16 usual prostrations.

10. Trisagion with prostrations and, after "Our Father", – "Lord, have mercy" (12) and prayer "All-Holy Trinity".

11. "O All-holy Trinity" and "Blessed be the name of the Lord" (3) with prostrations.

12. Glory, Both now: Psalm "I will bless the Lord"

13. *“It is truly meet”* and a prostration; Glory, Both now: "Lord, have mercy" (2), "Lord, bless".

3. **Dismissal:** Dismissal "O Christ our true God" with the commemoration of the service of the day and the saint

AT Great Compline

At the usual time of Vespers we sing Great Compline with prostrations, as we mentioned for Tuesday and Thursday evening of Cheesefare week, here on page 327

On Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday of the first week of Great Lent, after "O come, let us worship", we recite Psalm 69 "O God, come to my assistance", given in the order of Great Compline after the 3rd "O come, let us worship", after the prayer "O Master God the Father"; then one fourth part of each ode of the Great Canon (Matins on Thursday before the 5th Sunday of Lent)[^524]. Refrain to the troparia of the canon – "Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me"[^525], to the troparion of St. Mary of Egypt – "Venerable Mother Mary, pray to God for us", and to the troparion of St. Andrew – "Venerable Father Andrew, pray to God for us". According to the rubric, 3 small prostrations should be made at each troparion of the canon, however, among us this is not done, since there are no people in church at that time

The rubric for Great Compline we have partly here on page 327, and partly – in the *Horologion*.

### 4.1.8 Vespers on Wednesday and Friday with Presanctified

> **Note ** on Prostrations

On Wednesday we make 3 small prostrations: at the Trisagion at the beginning, at "O come, let us worship", at "Alleluia" after the pre-introductory psalm and after each antiphon of the Kathisma and at "Let my prayer be set forth". Great prostrations, according to local custom, we make at "Light of Christ", when the Priest blesses the people crosswise with the triple-candle; at the conclusion of the singing "Let my prayer be set forth" and after "Now the Powers of Heaven", when the consecrated Lamb is taken from the artophorion and placed on the diskos[^526]. And on Fridays at Vespers and at Compline we do not make prostrations, only the prescribed ones at the Presanctified, that is: after "Let my prayer be set forth" – 3 prostrations[^527], after the Entrance of the Holy Gifts – 3 prostrations and at "Let my prayer be set forth" – 3 prostrations, and among us also at "Light of Christ" – 3 prostrations.

After "Blessed is the Kingdom" we recite "O Heavenly King", Trisagion (with prostrations) and, after "Our Father", – "Lord, have mercy" (12), Glory, Both now: "O come, let us worship" three times (with prostrations)

Of the eight prayers recited at the prefatory psalm, the Priest recites here only the last 5, for the first three he has to read afterwards, one at each of the three antiphons of the Kathisma

3. 18th Kathisma, with a prayer at each of its three antiphons and with a Small Litany after each antiphon.

4. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: *Triodion* on 6 and *Menaion* on 4, Glory, Both now: Theotokion of the *Menaion*. If there is a Doxastikon of the saint, then we select the Theotokion in His tone. (On Friday evening stichera: Idiomelon of the *Triodion* twice, Martyria of the *Octoechos* of the current tone – 4[^528] and of the Saint – 4, Glory: of the saint, if there is one, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the departing tone; if not, then Glory, Both now: the same Theotokion)

5. **Entrance:** Entrance with the Censer (on the Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner, on the 40 Martyrs and on Great Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday entrance – with the Gospel)

At "O Gladsome Light" – Prokimenon of the *Triodion*, one reading of the *Triodion* and the second Prokimenon of the *Triodion*[^529]; then the Priest, having taken the triple-candle with the censer and exclaiming "Wisdom, Aright", begins "The Light of Christ", blessing with the triple-candle crosswise to the east, then, blessing to the west, says: "Illumines all"[^530]; all make three prostrations to the ground, and the Reader sings: "The Reading from Proverbs" and, when the Priest or Deacon exclaims: "Let us attend", reads the second reading of the *Triodion*

7. "Let my prayer be set forth". Has after it three verses and is sung six times, that is: twice – before the first verse, once – after each verse and again once at the end. And among us the first time "Let my prayer be set forth" is sung by the Priest, the second time – by the Choir, all three verses – by the Priest, after each the Choir – "Let my prayer be set forth", the last time in a higher voice up to the half – the Priest, and from the half – the Choir. Where there are two choirs, they sing "Let my prayer be set forth" alternately: the first begins after the Priest, and the second half is sung by both choirs together. When the Priest sings, he himself stands, and the Choir and people kneel; when the Choir sings, the Choir stands together with the people, and the Priest kneels. If there are two choirs, the one singing stands, and the other kneels; people who are on the side of the right choir kneel, stand and sing with the right choir, and those on the left – with the left[^531].

The Priest sings "Let my prayer be set forth" first in front of the altar, then the 1st verse – on the south, the 2nd – on the west, the 3rd – on the north side, and at the end the first half – again in front of the holy table[^532]. He censes each side of the altar twice, that is before the beginning of his singing and at the end of the Choir's singing, that is at "The lifting up of my hands", for then, having censed, he moves to the next side of the altar, in order to cense there also, so that the Choir is ready to sing its verse[^533].

Immediately after the end of the singing of "Let my prayer be set forth" is exclaimed "Let us all say" and according to the order – Liturgy of the Presanctified

> **Notes** 

If there is no Liturgy of the Presanctified, then we sing Vespers according to the rubric of Monday, Tuesday and Thursday evening, that is from the 10 stichera on *“Lord, I have cried”* we transfer the first 3 to the Aposticha, and the other 6 we sing on *“Lord, I have cried”*[^534]; and there will be on Wednesday stichera of the *Triodion* – 3 and of the *Menaion* – 3, and on Friday Martyria of the *Octoechos* – 3 and of the *Menaion* – 3. On Friday evening, after "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", there will be no Lenten troparia with prostrations, but the Troparion of the Saint, Glory, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones, in the tone of the Troparion of the Saint and, after the litany "Have mercy on us, O God", – 3 great prostrations[^535] and the Great Dismissal, as usual

If on this day falls a saint with Polyeleos, namely the Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner and the 40 Martyrs, and also on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of Passion Week[^536], then immediately after "Let my prayer be set forth" there will be censing and on the two previously named feasts their Epistle and Gospel are read, the Gospel – beginning from "Wisdom, Aright". On the three days of Passion Week only the Gospel is read, beginning from "And that we may be accounted worthy", since there is no Epistle

By the decision of the Synod of Lviv, the pastor must celebrate the Liturgy of the Presanctified on every Wednesday and every Friday of Great Lent and on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of Passion Week

> **Note ** on the number of prostrations per day. The number of prostrations made in church reached once 300 per day, excluding the Midnight Office: "Three hundred during the day and night, without the Midnight Office". (Greek *Triodion*, our Manuscript Typikon and *Tserkovne Oko* on the 1st Monday of Lent).

### 4.1.9 First Saturday of Great Lent

Memory of the Holy Great Martyr Theodore the Tyro[^537]

#### On Friday Evening

##### At Vespers

WITH PRESANCTIFIED: Everything according to the general rubric, here on page 349.

##### At Compline

Note

Compline on all Fridays of Great Lent, according to the Greek rubric, is Small, and according to the Pochaiv *Triodion*, *Tserkovne Oko* and the Moscow Typikon – Great. However, in our times, when abbreviations prevail, we should adhere to the Greek rubric, the more so because even in our Horologia, in the order of Great Compline, troparia are given only for 4 days of the week, that is for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. We do not make prostrations, as was already said on page 349.

1. If it be Small Compline, then after *“It is truly meet”* we recite the Kontakion of the Great Martyr; if Great, then after the 1st Trisagion – Troparion of the Great Martyr, Glory, Both now: Theotokion (Sunday, in the tone of the Troparion of the Saint)[^538]; after the 2nd Trisagion – usual troparia "Have mercy on us, O Lord"; after *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion of the Great Martyr, and the Troparion "O Lord of Hosts" we do not recite[^539]

##### At Compline

we sing the Canon for the Dead, which is in the *Octoechos* for the current tone, and the Canons of the *Menaion* to the saints of the nearest Saturday and Sunday we sing, if the Ecclesiarch prefers, one – at Compline on Friday with the Canon for the Dead, and the other – on Sunday at Compline[^540]. The Greek *Triodion* adds: "we do so on all Friday evenings of holy and Great Lent". Before the Canon for the Dead we should sing also the usual Theotokion Canon of the *Octoechos*, for the rubric does not exclude it[^541]

##### At Matins

1. From the beginning to the canon everything – according to the general rubric for a saint without Polyeleos on Saturday, except the 2nd Sessional Hymn, which will not be of the *Octoechos*, but of the *Triodion* of St. Theodore

2. **Canons:** Canons 3 on 14: Temple with heirmos on 6 and two of Theodore on 8. Katavasia after each ode – "I shall open"

After the 3rd Ode – Sessional Hymn of the Saint, after the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint, after the 9th – Exaposteilarion of the Saint.

3. **Praises (Lauds):** Stichera of the Praises to the Saint on 4, Doxastikon – to him, and Theotokion – in the *Triodion*

4. **After the Great Doxology:** Small Doxology and, after "Let us complete", – Aposticha of the Saint with his two verses and the subsequent order of Matins according to the rubric for a saint without Polyeleos on Saturday

##### At the Hours

At all: Troparion and Kontakion to the Saint.

##### At the Divine Liturgy

Everything – to the Saint, and the Epistle and Gospel first – of the day, and then – of the Saint.

### 4.1.10 First Sunday of Great Lent

Of Orthodoxy

[^542]Notes

The *Triodion* service of this Sunday has neither an All-Night Vigil nor a Polyeleos[^543], but is combined with the Sunday service of the *Octoechos*

The service of a saint without Polyeleos we sing at Compline or on another day

##### At Great Vespers

1. *“Blessed is the man”*, as usual.

1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: Sunday of the *Octoechos* – 6 and of the *Triodion* – 4, Glory: *Triodion*, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone (Dogmatikon)

2. Sunday Aposticha, Glory: *Triodion*, Both now: *Triodion*

3. At the end: Sunday Troparion, Glory: "We venerate Thy most pure image", Tone 2; Both now: Sunday Theotokion in the same Tone 2

##### At Compline

After *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion of the *Triodion* only.

##### At Great Matins

1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Sunday Troparion twice, Glory: "We venerate Thy most pure image", Both now: Sunday Theotokion in the same Tone 2

2. Everything else up to the canon – Sunday, as usual, only "Glory" will be *“Open to me the doors”*, Both now: *“Lead me on the paths of salvation”* and at "Have mercy on me, O God": *“Thinking upon the multitude”*

3. **Canons:** Canons 3 on 14: *Octoechos* Sunday on 4, Cross-Resurrection on 2, Theotokos on 2 and *Triodion* on 6[^544]. Katavasia of the *Triodion*

After the 3rd Ode – Sessional Hymn of the *Triodion*; after the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos of the *Triodion*; after the 9th – Sunday Exaposteilarion, Glory: *Triodion*, Both now: *Triodion*.

Stichera of the Praises – 9: 5 of the *Octoechos* and 4 of the *Triodion*, the three last – of the *Triodion*, Both now: *“Most Blessed Art Thou”*.

4. **After the Great Doxology:** Sunday Troparion, one of the two usual ones

5. After the dismissal – Glory, Both now: Gospel Sticheron

##### At the Hours

At all – Sunday Troparion, Glory: "We venerate Thy most pure image", Kontakion of the *Triodion*.

##### At the Divine Liturgy

1. **Troparia:** Troparion Sunday and "We venerate Thy most pure image", Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the *Triodion*[^545].

2. Everything else – of Orthodoxy, only Communion Hymn – "Praise the Lord" and "Rejoice in the Lord"

MONDAY, TUESDAY, WEDNESDAY, THURSDAY AND FRIDAY

### 4.1.11 Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday of the Second Week of Great Lent

Everything – according to the rubric for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday of the 1st week of Great Lent, here on page 347 and following.

Note

Let it be known that from this Monday of the 2nd week of Lent the canons of the saints in the *Menaion*, which fall from the Saturday of Lazarus to the Sunday of Ap. Thomas, are sung at Compline with the Theotokion Canons. First the Canon of the Theotokos is sung, and after it – the Canon of the *Menaion*. After the 3rd Ode – Kontakion and Sessional Hymn of the *Menaion*, and after the 6th – Sessional Hymn of the Theotokos; after the canon – Stichera of the *Menaion* (*Triodion* of this day).

### 4.1.12 Saturday of the Second Week of Great Lent

Note

The service of this Saturday, as also the services of the 3rd and 4th Saturdays of Great Lent, differ from the services of Meatfare Saturday and the Saturday before the Sunday of Pentecost in that it does not exclude fully either the service of the *Menaion*, or the service of the day of the *Octoechos*, that is to all saints and the dead. The services of Meatfare Saturday and the Saturday before the Sunday of Pentecost exclude generally the service of the *Menaion*, and from the service of the *Octoechos* little is taken, but have their own order in the *Triodion* exclusively for the dead. Therefore, we suppose that the two litanies for the dead: "In peace let us pray to the Lord" and "Have mercy on us, O God", which according to our later rubric are given at Vespers and at Matins, and the litany for the dead "Again and again", which is said between the odes of the canon, should be taken only on these two Saturdays which are exclusively for the dead, and on the other three – usual litanies.

##### At Vespers

WITH PRESANCTIFIED

1. 18th Kathisma.

1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: Idiomelon of the *Triodion* of the day twice, 4 Martyria of the *Octoechos* and 4 of the *Menaion* of the saint, Glory: of the saint, if there be, but if not, then Glory: Sticheron for the Dead of the tone, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the departing tone

2. Instead of the Prokimenon of the day of the *Horologion* there will be Prokimenon of the *Triodion* and reading, second Prokimenon and second reading of the *Triodion*, then "Let my prayer be set forth" and the rest of the Presanctified

> **Notes** 

3. After the end of the Presanctified, in other services of this day (except the Panakhida for the dead) vestments of red color should rather be used, than black, for red ones are – predominantly for martyrs

4. If there be no Presanctified, then we sing Vespers according to the rubric given here, on page 347

##### At Compline

Compline, according to the Greek rubric, we sing Small. After *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion of the *Triodion* *“With the saints give rest”*[^546].

Midnight Office – Saturday.

##### At Matins

1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Instead of *“God is the Lord”* we sing Alleluia in Tone 2 with verses

2. **Troparia:** Troparion of the day "Apostles, prophets" twice; Glory: "Remember, O Lord", Both now: Theotokion "Holy Mother"

3. **Kathisma:** After the 1st Kathisma – Small Litany and Sessional Hymn of the *Octoechos* of the current tone

4. 17th Kathisma ("The Blameless"), in two stations, with refrains and troparia

5. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons 3 on 14: of the Temple of the Lord or Theotokos with heirmos on 6, of the Saint of the *Menaion* on 4 and of the *Octoechos* of the current tone the second[^547] on 4. If the Temple is of a Saint, then – Canon of the Saint with heirmos on 6, Temple on 4 and Octoechos on 4. From the 6th Ode, leaving the Canons of the Temple and Octoechos, we sing the Canon of the Saint of the *Menaion* on 6 and both canons of the tetraodion on 8. Refrain to the troparia of the tetraodion – "Holy Martyrs, pray to God for us". At the end of the eight troparia of each ode of the tetraodion we add two more troparia: one Martyric with the Martyric refrain, and the second – for the dead with the refrain for the dead. From the two Martyric refrains "Wondrous is God" and "To the saints that are in His earth" and from the two refrains for the dead "Their souls" and "Blessed are they Whom Thou Hast chosen", the first we refrain to the Martyric and for the dead of the 6th and 8th Odes, and the second – to the Martyric and for the dead of the 7th and 9th Odes.
   * *Katavasia:* Katavasia after Odes 3, 6, 7, 8, and 9 – Heirmos of the last canon: after the 3rd – of the *Octoechos*, after the others – of the *Triodion*

After the 3rd Ode – Sessional Hymn of the Saint[^548], after the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos for the Dead, after the 9th – Exaposteilarion of the *Octoechos* (to all saints, Glory: to the dead).

6. **Praises (Lauds):** Stichera of the Praises, Martyria of the *Octoechos* – 4, Glory: for the Dead, Both now: Theotokion of the "Glory"

7. **After the Great Doxology:** After the Small Doxology at the Aposticha – Stichera for the Dead of the *Octoechos* with their verses for the dead

8. At the end: Troparion to all saints ("Apostles, prophets, martyrs"), Glory: "Remember, O Lord", Both now: "O Holy Mother of the Ineffable Light" and Dismissal.

##### At the Hours

At all – Troparion of the day ("Apostles, prophets"), Glory: "Remember, O Lord", Kontakion *“With the saints give rest”*.

##### At the Divine Liturgy

1. **Troparia:** "Apostles, prophets" and "Remember, O Lord"; Glory: Kontakion *“With the saints give rest”*, Both now: "Thee as a wall and haven"

2. Everything else – of the day and of the dead

### 4.1.13 Second Sunday of Great Lent

Everything – according to the general rubric for a saint without Polyeleos on Sunday, here on [pp. 47-54](#general-rubric-for-a-saint-without-polyeleos-on-sunday), only:

##### At Great Vespers

On *“Lord, I have cried”* there will be 6 Sunday stichera of the *Octoechos* and 4 to the saint of the *Menaion*.

##### At Compline

After *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion of the *Triodion*.

##### At Great Matins

1. Before the Canon we sing *“Open to me the doors”* and the rest, as on the first Sunday of Lent

2. **Canons:** Canons: Sunday of the current tone with heirmos on 6, *Triodion* on 4 and Saint of the *Menaion* on 4

After the 3rd Ode – Kontakion and Ikos of the Sunday and to the Saint, if he has one; Glory: his Sessional Hymn, Both now: his Theotokion; after the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos of the *Triodion*.

3. **Praises (Lauds):** 9: Sunday of the *Octoechos* on 8, with the usual verses of the Praises psalms, one of the *Triodion* with the verse "Arise, O Lord my God", then Glory: and again the same sticheron; Both now: *“Most Blessed Art Thou”*

4. At the end of Matins – Glory, Both now: Gospel Sticheron

##### At the Hours

Instead of the Sunday Kontakion we read the Kontakion of the *Triodion*, the rest – according to the general rubric.

##### At the Divine Liturgy

1. Instead of the Sunday Kontakion we sing the Kontakion of the *Triodion*

2. Sunday Prokimenon of the current tone and the rest – according to the general rubric

### 4.1.14 Third Week of Great Lent

Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday

Everything – according to the general Lenten rubric given for the first week of Great Lent, here from p. 347.

Third Saturday of Great Lent

Everything – according to the rubric of the second Saturday of Great Lent, here on page 357.

THIRD SUNDAY OF GREAT LENT – VENERATION OF THE CROSS

> **Notes** 

The service of a saint without Polyeleos we sing at Compline

The entire divine service, according to the Synod of Lviv, should be celebrated in violet vestments (according to the previous – in purple)

##### At Great Vespers

1. *“Blessed is the man”*, as usual.

1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: 6 Sunday of the *Octoechos* and 4 of the *Triodion*; Glory: *Triodion*, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone

2. Sunday Aposticha; Glory, Both now: *Triodion*

3. At the end: Sunday Troparion, Glory: of the Cross, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones, in the tone of the Cross

4. **Dismissal:** "Christ our true God, Who rose from the dead, through the prayers of His most pure Mother, by the power of the precious and life-giving Cross, which we venerate today, through the intercessions of the holy, glorious and all-laudable apostles, of our venerable and God-bearing fathers and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind"

BRINGING OUT OF THE PRECIOUS CROSS FROM

THE SACRISTY TO THE ALTAR

The bringing out of the Precious Cross from the sacristy to the altar takes place after the dismissal of Vespers, according to the rubric given for September 14, here on [pp. 121-122](#14-september--exaltation-of-the-precious-and-life-giving-cross).

##### At Compline

After *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion to the Cross "No longer does the flaming sword guard".

##### At Great Matins

1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Sunday Troparion twice, Glory: to the Cross, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones in the tone of the Cross

2. Everything else up to the canon – Sunday, as usual, only after the 50th Psalm we sing *“Open to me the doors”* and the rest

3. **Canons:** Canons 3 on 14: *Octoechos* Sunday with heirmos on 4, Theotokos on 2 and *Triodion* on 8. Katavasia of the *Triodion*

After the 3rd Ode – Sessional Hymn of the Cross; after the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos of the Cross; after the 9th – Sunday Exaposteilarion, Glory: of the Cross, Both now: Theotokion of the Cross.

4. **Praises (Lauds):** 9: 4 Sunday of the *Octoechos* and 5 of the *Triodion*, of which the three last – with the verses of the Cross; Glory: once more the last sticheron of the *Triodion*, Both now: *“Most Blessed Art Thou”*

5. **After the Great Doxology:** During the Great Doxology the bringing out of the Precious Cross from the altar to the tetrapod takes place, according to the rubric given here on [pp. 122-123](#14-september--bringing-out-of-the-precious-cross); then veneration, immediately after the singing of the troparion "Save, O Lord", for then the Priest begins to sing the troparion "Before Thy Cross" (3) and there will be veneration in such a way as given here on [pp. 124-127](#14-september--veneration-of-the-precious-cross)

6. After the dismissal – Glory, Both now: Gospel Sticheron

##### At the Hours

At all – Sunday Troparion, Glory: of the Cross. Kontakion – only of the Cross.

##### At the Divine Liturgy

1. **Troparia:** Troparion Sunday and of the Cross; Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Cross

2. Instead of the Trisagion we sing "Before Thy Cross"

3. Everything else – only of the Cross

> **Note ** on the Veneration of the Precious Cross

After the dismissal of the Liturgy, and also after the end of every service celebrated in church, from this day until the end of the 6th Hour of the following Friday, veneration of the Precious Cross takes place: the Priest, having come before the tetrapod, sings together with the people "Before Thy Cross we bow down" (3). If there be a sufficient number of people, the Choir sings the stichera of veneration until all have venerated, according to the rubric given on page 127, in the note[^549].

Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday

of the fourth week of Great Lent

Everything – according to the general Lenten rubric of the previous weeks, except the veneration of the Precious Cross, according to the previously stated. Only Wednesday and Friday differ from the other three days in that at Matins, instead of the Canon of the *Menaion*, they have the Cross Canon of the *Triodion*. Also at Vespers on Tuesday for Wednesday all 6 stichera on *“Lord, I have cried”* will be of the Cross; and the Canon of the *Menaion* on these two days we take at Compline.

### 4.1.15 Fourth Saturday of Great Lent

Everything – according to the rubric of the second Saturday of Great Lent, here on page 357.

### 4.1.16 Fourth Sunday of Great Lent

Everything – according to the rubric of the second Sunday of Great Lent, here on page 360.

Note

The service of St. John of the Ladder, which some later [typika] prescribed to sing on this Sunday, is usually not taken among us. And if someone, namely in monasteries, wishes to sing it, let him sing it instead of the service of the regular saint of the *Menaion*, according to the rubric for a saint without Polyeleos on 4, and let him take the service of the regular saint at Compline. According to this Typikon, the service of St. Mary of Egypt is sung on the fifth[^550] Sunday of Lent, but if someone wishes, he may sing it instead of the service of the regular saint.

### 4.1.17 Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday of the Fifth Week of Great Lent

Everything – according to the general Lenten rubric of past weeks.

Thursday of the fifth week of Great Lent

on which we sing the Great Canon

The service of the regular saint is transferred to another day.

#### On Wednesday Evening

##### At Vespers

WITH PRESANCTIFIED

Everything – according to the Lenten rubric, as usual, except the stichera on *“Lord, I have cried”*, which are taken 28 on 29, for the first Idiomelon is repeated, also one more at "Glory" and one at "Both now".

Refrains to the first 20 stichera we take from *“Lord, I have cried”*, beginning from "Fall into their own nets"; to the 21st and 22nd stichera we refrain two usual verses from the Aposticha of Vespers; and to the other seven – "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee".

> **Notes** 

1. The stichera, not only the two first, but also all others, we sing in the tone of the Idiomela, for of the three types of Prosomoia given in the *Triodion* at the other stichera, two in our Heirmologia we do not find; and the one which is given at the stichera of St. Andrew of Crete, although it is given also in the Heirmologia, nevertheless, today we do not use. The stichera of St. Andrew of Crete, in the Greek text are given according to the order and in the sequence of the 24 letters of the Greek alphabet

2. If there be no Presanctified, then the Idiomelon and Martyricon stichera on *“Lord, I have cried”* are not taken, but are transferred with their two refrains to the Aposticha

3. It is not good to neglect prostrations at the stichera of St. Andrew

4. At the entire divine service of this day we use sacred vestments of Lenten colors, as usual

##### At Compline

We sing Small, without prostrations. After *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion of the Great Canon.

Midnight Office: Without prostrations. After the 1st Trisagion – usual troparia, after the 2nd – Kontakion of the Great Canon.

##### At Matins

1. From the beginning to the end of the Sessional Hymns of the *Octoechos*, given at the end of the *Triodion*, at the 1st Kathisma, we sing everything according to the general Lenten rubric, then Psalm 50 and immediately, having omitted the litany "Save, O God", the Great Canon[^551]. At the time of the singing of the canon the holy doors are opened and candles are lit on the holy table. Before the holy doors in cathedral churches a rug is spread, on which first the Bishop, if he be present, and then the other sacred ministers two by two, according to the rank of their dignity, at each ode make one great prostration, after the singing of each troparion of the ode of the canon. In our seminary, the seminarians make prostrations before the holy doors, and in the sanctuary, before the steps of the altar, all eight superiors make prostrations according to the rank of their dignity, one at one ode, by turn, and at the 9th Ode – all eight together, in epitrachelia

2. **Canons:** Canons two: one – the Great [Canon] of St. Andrew, of nine odes, the second – triodion, contains the 4th, 8th and 9th Odes, which also in these odes takes the first place. The odes of the nine-ode canon do not have an equal number of troparia and each of them has at the end two troparia to St. Mary of Egypt and one to St. Andrew of Crete. The triodion we sing on 10 troparia with the first heirmos, for the 2nd heirmos is not sung. Refrains to the troparia of the Great Canon are these: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", then "Venerable Father Andrew, pray to God for us", then "Venerable Mother Mary, pray to God for us". To the troparia of the triodion the refrain will be – "Holy Apostles, pray to God for us"[^552], because according to content they belong to the service of Thursday. At each troparion of the Canon of St. Andrew the rubrics prescribe three prostrations, but we make only one, however, great, and in cathedral temples the clergy makes prostrations only by turn and adapted to the nine odes of the canon. The choirs sing the canon in the middle of the church, each at a separate analogion, making at the troparia of the canon a small prostration. As Katavasia at all odes we take the heirmos of the last canon[^553]

After the 3rd Ode – Sessional Hymn of the *Triodion*, after the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos of the *Triodion* with the Beatitudes; after the 9th – Trinity Sessional Hymn, all this – with the usual litanies. At the 9th Ode we sing "More honorable", as the Moscow and the new Constantinopolitan Typika also have. After the Canon – *“It is truly meet”*[^554].

3. Everything else, from the Praises psalms to the end of Matins, is taken according to the general Lenten rubric, only, if we do not add the 1st Hour, then after the 16 final prostrations at the prayer of St. Ephrem we recite the Trisagion with "Our Father" and "Lord, have mercy" (12), and then the Priest: "Glory to Thee, O Christ God" and dismissal

##### At the Hours

Everything – according to the usual Lenten rubric, however, after the Trisagion we recite at all Hours only the one Kontakion of the Canon, and the 1st Hour – without Kathisma.

AT THE TYPIKA AND AT VESPERS: Everything – according to the usual Lenten rubric.

LITURGY

According to the rubric there should be the Presanctified, however, now we do not sing it during Great Lent, with the exception of Wednesdays and Fridays. In the archcathedral church on this day only read liturgies are celebrated.

FIFTH SATURDAY OF GREAT LENT – OF THE AKATHIST[^555]

Note

The service of this feast is of the small type; it has only the Katavasia at Matins after each ode and the Great Doxology and is combined with the usual service of Lenten Saturday and with the Temple Canon at Matins. The peculiarity of this feast lies in that at its Matins the whole order of the Akathist to the Most Pure Virgin Mary is sung, the 12 ikos-Kontakia of which are divided into four quarters, the first of which is sung instead of the Sessional Hymn after the first Kathisma, the second – instead of the Sessional Hymn – after the second Kathisma, the third – after the 3rd, and the fourth – after the 6th Ode of the Canon; the initial Kontakion is sung at the beginning and at the end of each quarter, and before the last singing of it – once more the first Ikos[^556]. This Matins, according to the rubric, is sung at the 4th hour of the night, but we sing it at the usual time[^557]. The service of the regular saint, according to the rubric of the Greek *Triodion*, is sung at Compline.

##### At Vespers

WITH PRESANCTIFIED

1. **Kathisma:** "usual

2. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* stichera on 10: Idiomelon of the day twice, one Martyric and of the feast on 7, Glory, Both now: of the feast

3. At "O Gladsome Light" – Prokimenon of the *Triodion* and reading, second Prokimenon of the *Triodion* and reading and the rest of the Presanctified

Small Compline: After *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion of the feast only[^560].

Midnight Office – Saturday.

##### At Matins

1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Troparion of the feast twice; Glory, Both now: once more

2. **Kathisma:** After the 1st Kathisma – Small Litany and the initial Kontakion "To the Directress" is sung by the Choir. The Priest, dressed in all sacred vestments of light color, opens the holy doors and censes everything as usual; then, having come to the altar, sings the first quarter of the ikos-Kontakia and, after its conclusion, the same choir sings once more the initial Kontakion "To the Directress". All rubrics at this singing prescribe standing; (and therefore this is called Akathist, that is non-sitting). The Choir sings the Kontakion in the middle of the church majestically and solemnly

3. **Kathisma:** After the 2nd Kathisma and after the 3rd and 6th Odes of the Canon, immediately after the Small Litany, the Priest sings the other three quarters of the ikos-Kontakia, and the Choir – the Kontakion "To the Directress" at the beginning and at the end of each quarter. At the beginning of each quarter the Priest censes everything just as at the beginning of the first quarter[^558]

This Akathist order is celebrated usually at the altar. In the cathedral temple it is sung at the altar of the Mother of God, which is located in its right nave; and then the Priest censes the altar and everything else, as usual, and immediately, having left the holy doors open, goes out through them to the altar of the Most Holy Theotokos and sings there the Akathist order, censing from the altar at the beginning of each quarter the icon of the Mother of God, the sacred ministers, the choirs and the people. After singing the 4th quarter of the ikos-Kontakia the Priest returns to the sanctuary, closes the holy doors and goes to the sacristy, where he takes off the sacred vestments and, having put on the epitrachelion, continues the service of Matins.

4. **Canons:** Canons 2 on 12: Temple of the Saint with heirmos on 6 and of the feast on 6. Katavasia "I shall open my mouth" up to the 6th Ode. From the 6th Ode we do not take the Canon of the Temple, but we sing 3 canons on 14, that is of the feast on 6 and both canons of the triodion on 8 with the addition of two troparia, that is one Martyric with the refrain "Wondrous is God", and the second – for the dead, with the refrain "Their souls", and the Katavasia of the *Triodion*. Refrain to the troparia of the Canon of the Theotokos – the general "Most Holy Theotokos, save us", however, among us they like to refrain the acrostic of the canon "Container of Joy, to Thee alone it is fitting to rejoice". In Greek: "Vessel of joy, to Thee alone it is fitting to rejoice". Both the troparia and this refrain we sing to the melody given in the new *Heirmologion* on the Akathist Saturday

After the 3rd Ode, after the last singing of the Kontakion "To the Directress", we recite the SESSIONAL HYMN of the feast; after the 6th, immediately after the Small Litany, is sung the last quarter of the ikos-Kontakia with the Kontakion "To the Directress" before the beginning and after the conclusion, however, its last Kontakion "O All-praised Mother" is sung three times, after this – the 1st Ikos and then – "To the Directress". At the 9th Ode we sing "More honorable" and after the 9th – Exaposteilarion of the feast.

5. **Praises (Lauds):** 4: all – of the feast, Glory, Both now: of the feast

6. **After the Great Doxology:** Troparion of the feast

##### At the Hours

AND AT THE LITURGY: Everything – only of the feast; only the Epistle and Gospel first – of the day, and then – of the feast.

### 4.1.18 Fifth Sunday of Great Lent

Everything – according to the rubric of the 2nd Sunday, here on page 360.

MONDAY, TUESDAY, WEDNESDAY, THURSDAY AND FRIDAY

### 4.1.19 Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday of the Sixth Week of Great Lent

Everything – according to the general rubric of past weeks.

## 4.2 Flower Triodion (Pentecostarion)

PRESCRIPTIONS OF THE SYNOD OF LVIV TO PASTORS

ON DIVINE WORSHIP

FROM THE SATURDAY OF LAZARUS TO BRIGHT TUESDAY

INCLUSIVE

On the Saturday before Flowery Sunday, called Lazarus [Saturday], let the Liturgy be sung in church

On Flowery Sunday let everything be celebrated as usual, according to the rubric of a feast of the Lord of the first rank with the addition of the blessing of branches at Matins

On the three following days of Great Week it is fitting to sing the Liturgy of the Presanctified

On Thursday of Passion Week it is fitting to sing the Liturgy together with Vespers

On the same day, after sunset, it is fitting to sing the Office of the "Passions" with the 12 Gospels

On Friday, which we mark as a solemn feast, let the Hours be celebrated in the morning in church, called Royal, and about noon – Vespers with the bringing out of the Shroud[^559], which, when it is brought out, is placed before the iconostasis in the so-called tomb, and there let it remain for constant veneration by the people until Resurrection Matins

It would be very desirable that the pastors on the same day, after the placing of the Shroud, preach to the people at a convenient time a word on the passion and death of Christ

It is also entrusted to the same pastors to celebrate on this Friday, after sunset, Tomb Matins in church, in view of the divine service of this day and in view of the solemn rites celebrated at its end

On Great Saturday itself it is fitting to sing the Liturgy of St. Basil with Vespers

On the Sunday of the Resurrection very early it is fitting to sing Matins with all the rites that precede and accompany it, according to the rubric approved by this Synod. In cathedral churches, similarly as in non-cathedral ones, this Matins is usually anticipated and celebrated on Saturday evening; the Synod considers that such a custom may be adhered to

On the first three days of Bright Week it is fitting daily to sing Matins, Liturgy and Vespers in church

The Synod forbids all priests read liturgies throughout the whole Passion Week, and on the first three days of this week prescribes only the Liturgy of the Presanctified; on Great Thursday and Saturday – only the sung Liturgy, that is of St. Basil the Great with Vespers (Title IV, Chapter I. 3. 5). On Great Friday, with the exception of the feast of the Annunciation, the Liturgy should not be celebrated

Note

From this Saturday to the Sunday of Ap. Thomas inclusive only the *Triodion* is sung, and the *Menaion* – only if the Annunciation falls, and from Bright Monday to the Sunday of Ap. Thomas inclusive, if a saint with Vigil or Polyeleos falls. The Canons of saints without Polyeleos of these 16 days are prescribed for Compline, beginning from Monday of the 2nd week of Great Lent, as was noted above, on page 357.

### 4.2.1 Lazarus Saturday

Note

The service of this feast is of the small type and only at Matins, from the Canon onwards, – great. However, also before the Canon it has some parts of the Sunday service, namely after the 2nd Kathisma, that is "The Blameless", it has "The Choir of angels", after the 2nd Sessional Hymn it has "The Resurrection of Christ" and before the Exaposteilarion – "Holy is the Lord our God" three times.

#### On Friday Evening

##### At Vespers

WITH PRESANCTIFIED

1. **Kathisma:** "proper

2. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: Idiomelon of the day twice, Martyricon once, then 7 of the feast, Glory, Both now: of the feast

3. At "O Gladsome Light" – Prokimenon of the *Triodion* and one reading of the *Triodion*, then 2nd Prokimenon, 2nd reading of the *Triodion* and everything else of the Presanctified

AT Small Compline

We sing the Canon of Lazarus in the *Triodion*, after the Canon, instead of *“It is truly meet”*, – Heirmos of the 9th Ode of the Canon. After the Trisagion – Kontakion of the feast only.

##### At the Midnight Office

After the 1st Trisagion, instead of the troparia "Uncreated Nature", we read the Troparion of Lazarus; after the 2nd Trisagion, instead of the troparia "Remember, O Lord", – Kontakion of Lazarus, and the prayer "Remember" we do not say.

##### At Matins

1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Troparion of the feast twice, Glory, Both now: the same

2. After the 1st and 2nd Kathismata – Sessional Hymn of the feast, however, after the 2nd Kathisma, before the Sessional Hymn, we sing "The Choir of angels" exactly as on Sunday; and after the Sessional Hymn – "The Resurrection of Christ", Psalm 50 and immediately Canon

3. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons of the feast – two: 1st – with heirmos on 8 and 2nd – on 6. From the 6th Ode – tetraodion, heirmos – twice, troparia – on 6, then the other canon on 6. 
   * *Katavasia:* Katavasia after each ode – Heirmos of the 2nd Canon. Refrain to the troparia – "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"[^561]. 
   * *After the 3rd Ode:* Sessional Hymn, 
   * *After the 6th Ode:* Kontakion and Ikos of the feast; at the 9th we do not sing "More honorable"; 
   * *After the 9th Ode:* we do not say *“It is truly meet”* until the Sunday of Ap. Thomas; 
   * *After the 9th Ode:* Exaposteilarion of the feast, however, before the Exaposteilarion we sing "Holy is the Lord our God" three times

4. **Praises (Lauds):** 8: all – of the feast, with two Sunday verses, as every Sunday; Glory: of the feast, Both now: *“Most Blessed Art Thou”*

5. **After the Great Doxology:** Troparion of the feast only

6. **Dismissal:** Dismissal specific

##### At the Hours

AND AT THE LITURGY: Everything – only of the feast, and at the Liturgy, instead of the Trisagion, we sing "All Who have been baptized into Christ".

### 4.2.2 Flower Sunday (Palm Sunday)

[^562]Everything – according to the general rubric of a feast of the Lord with All-Night Vigil without Litiya. It has everything proper to itself, and at the Liturgy – Antiphons and Entrance Hymn. However, before the Troparion of Flowery [Sunday] we sing yesterday's Troparion of Lazarus; only after the Great Doxology we sing the Troparion of Lazarus alone.

##### At Great Vespers

On *“Lord, I have cried”* – stichera on 10; and at the blessing of loaves – Troparion of Lazarus twice and of Flowery [Sunday] – once.

##### At Great Matins

1. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Troparion of Lazarus twice, Glory, Both now: of Flowery [Sunday]

2. The blessing and distribution of branches takes place, according to the rubric, immediately after the 50th Psalm, during the kissing of the Gospel. According to our custom, the blessing takes place after the 50th Psalm, and the distribution – during the anointing with oil (myrovanie), that is during the canon. And it takes place thus: When the Priest has sung the Gospel, he places it on the analogion near the tetrapod, between two candles lit on candlesticks. On the tetrapod are placed branches and prepared censers and sprinklers. The Priest approaches the tetrapod and at the time when the Choir reads the 50th Psalm, having put incense in and blessed the censer, censes the branches from the four sides of the tetrapod and, after the conclusion of the 50th Psalm, when the Deacon exclaims (if there be none, then the Priest himself) "Let us pray to the Lord", reads aloud (from the *Sluzhebnik* (lit. "Sluzhebnik") or from the *Triodion*[^563] ) the first prayer "O Lord our God", and the Choir responds: "Amen". Priest: "Peace be to all"; deacon: "Bow your heads unto the Lord"; and, after "To Thee, O Lord", the Priest reads the second prayer "O Lord God Almighty... unto ages of ages"[^564]; choir: "Amen"; the Priest sprinkles the branches with holy water, saying: "These branches are blessed and sanctified" and the rest; and, after singing the litany "Save, O God", with His right hand anoints the people, and with His left hand distributes to all the branches, which the Deacon solemnly hands to him, and if there be no deacon, then one of the church servers[^565]

After the 9th Ode we do not read the Exaposteilarion, but immediately: "Holy is the Lord our God" (3) in Tone 4.

##### At the Divine Liturgy

After the Entrance – Troparion of Lazarus, Glory: of FLOWERY [SUNDAY], Both now: Kontakion of FLOWERY [SUNDAY]. We sing the Trisagion.

FAST FOR THE WHOLE PASSION WEEK

On Monday, Wednesday and Friday the Synod of Lviv prescribes a strict fast. On Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday it permits also dairy products (Title XI, part 4).

### 4.2.3 Great Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday[^566]

> **Notes** 

The sacred vestments of these days and of the whole Passion Week, beginning from Flowery Sunday evening, should be of violet color

All these three days have one form of divine service, that is Lenten, as in the Forty Days [Lent], only with certain exceptions, as given below:

##### At Vespers

a) On Flowery Sunday evening

1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* stichera of the *Triodion* on 6, Glory: *Triodion*, Both now: *Triodion*

2. **Entrance:** Entrance, Prokimenon of the day ("Bless the Lord now") and immediately "Vouchsafe, O Lord"

3. **Aposticha:** Aposticha of the *Triodion* with specific verses

4. After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" with the Trisagion – Troparion "Virgin Theotokos" and everything else with prostrations, as on the previous Sundays of Great Lent

5. **Dismissal:** Dismissal specific, so also on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday at the end of the Hours: "Christ the Lord, Who goes"[^567]

b) On Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday evening

##### At Vespers

WITH PRESANCTIFIED

1. **On *"Lord, I have cried"*:* 10 stichera: all – of the *Triodion*, Glory, Both now: *Triodion*

2. **Entrance:** Entrance with the Gospel and, after "O Gladsome Light", – two Prokimena of the *Triodion*, each – with its reading

3. After "Let my prayer be set forth" the Priest: "And that we may be accounted worthy" and the rest and reads the Gospel of Matthew, Section 98 and the rest of the Presanctified with the dismissal "Christ the Lord, Who goes"

> **Note:** If there be no Presanctified, then on *“Lord, I have cried”* we sing stichera on 6, and the three last we transfer to the Aposticha with the usual verses, singing the first twice. We make the Entrance with the Gospel and, after the second reading of the *Triodion*, we sing the Gospel, as above, and everything else with prostrations, according to the Lenten custom.

##### At Compline

On Sunday evening we sing Small Compline, according to the rubric of other Sundays of Great Lent, and at it – the triodion of the *Triodion*, and after the Trisagion – Kontakion of the *Triodion* only.

On Monday and Tuesday evening – Great Compline with prostrations according to the Lenten rubric, and at it also – the triodion of the *Triodion* and after the Trisagion – Kontakion of the *Triodion*, then "O Lord of Hosts, be with us"[^568].

On Wednesday evening we sing Small Compline[^569], also at it – the triodion of the *Triodion* and, after the Trisagion, – Kontakion of the *Triodion* only.

##### At the Midnight Office

Nothing special.

##### At Matins

1. At Alleluia, instead of the Trinity Hymns, we sing the Troparion "Behold the Bridegroom" twice, Glory, Both now: the same

2. Three regular Kathismata with their Sessional Hymns, then "And that we may be accounted worthy", Gospel of Matins[^570], according to the sequence of Gospels, Psalm 50 and "Save, O God"[^571]

3. **Canons:** Canon only one: triodion on Monday and Wednesday, or diodion [two-ode canon] on Tuesday. Troparia – on 12, heirmoi – twice. We do not recite the [Biblical] Odes, but only the refrain to the troparia of the canon "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"[^572], then the Katavasia, heirmos of the canon once both choirs together. Before the Kontakion-Ikos the Priest sings the Small Litany; at the 9th Ode we do not sing "More honorable", nor *“It is truly meet”* after the canon, but immediately after the Katavasia – Small Litany and Exaposteilarion "Thy bridal chamber" twice, Glory, Both now: three times the same

4. **Praises (Lauds):** 4: of the *Triodion*, Glory, Both now: *Triodion*, Small Doxology and, after "Let us complete", – Aposticha of the *Triodion* and everything else with prostrations, as on the Lenten days of Great Lent

##### At the Hours

Everything – according to the general Lenten rubric of Great Lent, only:

1. At the 1st and 9th Hours there will be no Kathisma, but it will be only at the 3rd and 6th

2. Immediately after the Theotokion "O Theotokos, Thou Art the vine" at the 3rd Hour and, after the corresponding Theotokia, at the other two Hours, the rubrics prescribe the reading of the Four Gospels, which today among us is read only in cathedral, or conciliar, churches[^573]. At the 6th Hour we read the Gospel not immediately after the Theotokion, but after the conclusion of the Troparion of the Prophecy and the Paremia with its Prokimena. The reading of the Four Gospels covers all the Evangelists, that is Matthew, Mark and Luke in full, and John – only up to the "Passion of Christ", that is up to "Now is the Son of man glorified", Section 46, verse 13.32. All the Evangelists, taken together, are divided into 9 readings, according to the number of the three Hours (3, 6, 9) and three days (Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday). Matthew is divided into 2 readings, Mark – into 2, John – into 2, and Luke – into 3. The first reading covers the first half of Matthew, the second – the second half of Matthew, the third – the first half of Mark, the fourth – the second half of Mark, the fifth – the first part of Luke, the sixth – the second part of Luke, the seventh – the third part of Luke, the eighth – the first half of John, the ninth – the second half of John. The rubric does not indicate where the first half of the three Evangelists and the first and second parts of Luke end. But since Matthew has 28 chapters, its half ends with the 14th chapter, Mark – 16 chapters, so its half ends with the 8th chapter, Luke – 24 chapters, so its first part ends with the 8th chapter, and the second – with the 16th. John, up to "Now is [the Son of man] glorified", has 12 chapters and part of the 13th chapter, therefore its half ends with the 6th chapter and part of the 7th

The Priest, at the beginning of each reading, dressed in a phelonion of Lenten color, opens the holy doors and censes everything as usual, then, having come out through the holy doors to the analogion placed before the holy doors facing the people, on which stand two candlesticks with lit candles, reads from there the Gospel, beginning from "And that we may be accounted worthy". After the conclusion of each reading, having kissed the beginning of the reading and leaving the Gospel on the analogion until the end of the 3rd reading, he returns to the sanctuary and, having closed the holy doors, takes off the phelonion[^574].

3. After the Trisagion – Kontakion of the *Triodion*

AT THE TYPIKA

4. Only one Kontakion of the *Triodion*

5. In Slavonic rubrics and the Greek Typikon of Sabbas, on Great Wednesday, instead of the dismissal the prayer "O Master most merciful" is given, which is at Vespers with All-Night Vigil, and in Slavonic ones – also the prayer of forgiveness for sins committed in Great Lent, and commemorations. However, these superfluous additions of the Greco-Slavs are unknown to the Greeks. The prayer "O Master most merciful" and the forgiveness may be retained perhaps only in monasteries. The commemorations, which are superfluous here, will be taken later, at the end of Compline and the Midnight Office, which have nothing in common with forgiveness for the sins of the Forty Days

#### On Wednesday

##### At Vespers

WITH PRESANCTIFIED,

##### At Compline

AND AT THE Midnight Office

Everything – according to the rubric of Monday and Tuesday, here on [pp. 379-380](#great-monday-and-great-tuesday), only on Wednesday, after the dismissal of the Liturgy of the Presanctified, the prostrations in church cease, and in the cells are made until the ringing for Matins of the bright Resurrection of Christ[^575]. We, however, until the Resurrection of Christ make three great prostrations in church, at the end of the Divine Service, singing the verse "Though Thou didst suffer", and during the veneration of the Shroud, singing "The noble Joseph".

### 4.2.4 Great Thursday[^576]

##### At Matins

1. "Blessed is our God", "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", "O Heavenly King" and everything else, as usual, with the Two Psalms and with the Six Psalms up to the end of the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord".

2. **On *"God is the Lord"*:* Instead of *“God is the Lord”* we sing Alleluia in Tone 8, that is in the tone of the following troparion; but since this troparion has a specific melody in the *Heirmologion*, we sing Alleluia according to the pattern of its melody

3. **Troparia:** Troparion "When the glorious disciples" twice, Glory, Both now: once more the same

4. There will be no Kathismata and Sessional Hymns, but immediately the Gospel from Luke, Section 108 and 1st verse of Section 109, that is the 39th verse of the 22nd chapter[^577]; then Psalm 50 and, leaving out "Save, O God", we sing immediately the Canon

5. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canon only one: heirmoi – twice, troparia – on 6[^578] with the refrain "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee". 
   * *Katavasia:* Katavasia after each ode – heirmos of the same canon once, both choirs together. 
   * *After the 3rd Ode:* we recite the Sessional Hymn, 
   * *After the 6th Ode:* Kontakion and Ikos, at the 9th we do not sing "More honorable"[^579], nor 
   * *After the 9th Ode:* *“It is truly meet”*, but instead of this, – the heirmos of the canon[^580] and immediately the Exaposteilarion twice, Glory, Both now: the same

6. **Praises (Lauds):** Stichera of the Praises – 4 and, after the Small Doxology, – "Let us complete".

7. "It is a good thing" once, Trisagion with "Our Father" and Troparion "When the glorious disciples", without Theotokion.

8. Priest: "Wisdom"; Choir: "Bless"

Priest: "Blessed be He... ages"; Choir: "Amen"; and 1st Hour.

##### At the Hours

1. At all: Troparion and Kontakion of Great Thursday, however, at the 1st Hour, after the Theotokion "What shall we call Thee", we read the Troparion of the Prophecy, Prokimenon, Paremia and 2nd Prokimenon

2. **Dismissal:** The Dismissal "Christ the Lord, Who goes"[^581] we recite at the 1st Hour, and at the others, since they are sung together with the Typika, we recite this dismissal at the end of the Typika. All this we recite in our cells

AT THE TYPIKA

3. Begins from the Beatitudes, without stichera. The Creed may be omitted, since it will be at the Liturgy

4. Instead of the usual Kontakia we recite the Kontakion of Great Thursday

5. After the Kontakion – "Lord, have mercy" (40), "O All-holy Trinity"[^582] and dismissal

Great Thursday evening

##### At Vespers

WITH THE LITURGY OF ST. BASIL[^583]

Note

"It is fitting for the Priest on Great Thursday at the Liturgy to consecrate two Lambs, in order to consume one at Communion, and to place the other in the artophorion and keep in the tabernacle in the usual place until today (Friday)". Thus in our *Sluzhebnik*[^584]. Regarding the Lamb itself, which is to be kept in the tabernacle until the day of exposition, the Synod of Lviv orders that "it before consecration be fitted to its vessel, the so-called Melchizedek, into which it is well inserted and carefully wiped, so that afterwards crumbs do not fall from it; so that placed in such a way in the Melchizedek, it be consecrated at the Liturgy of one of the preceding days and kept in the tabernacle until the exposition itself".
