## Rubrics of the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts

30. On the Holy and Great Forty Days [Lent] at the Proskomedia of the Divine Liturgy on Sunday or on the last day before the Liturgy of Presanctified Gifts, besides the Lamb that is to be consecrated on that day, other Lambs are also prepared for those Liturgies of Presanctified Gifts that are to be celebrated on the following days. Having cut, sacrificed and pierced the first Lamb, the Priest performs the same rites also over the other Lambs, reciting at each of them: "In remembrance," "As a sheep," "Sacrificed," "One of the soldiers" and places them one near another on the diskos. Then he pours wine and water into the holy chalice, having recited what is prescribed and, according to custom, finishes the Proskomedia

31. When the Lamb is to be blessed at the invocation of the Holy Spirit, He says: "And make this Bread" in the singular, and not in the plural, for Christ is – only one

32. At the elevation he elevates simultaneously all consecrated Lambs; breaks only the first Lamb, places a part into the holy chalice and pours warm water when prescribed. After this he takes the other holy Lambs and places them in the pyx in the tabernacle

33. Then, according to custom, the Priest recites the prayers, communicates and finishes the sacrifice according to the prescription

### In Concelebration of One Deacon

1. For the reading of the Hours, the Priest in the epitrachelion stands before the holy doors and begins: "Blessed is our God."

> **Reader**: "Amen,"

"O Heavenly King" and the rest. After "Our Father" the Priest, having said the exclamation, enters the sanctuary through the southern doors. The 3rd, 6th, 9th Hours are read, as well as the Typika.

2. At the end of the Typika the Priest and deacon vest in the sacred vestments as usual, but putting on each [vestment] they say nothing more, but only "Let us pray to the Lord."

3. When the Reader finishes the Typika, having recited the Trisagion, "Our Father," "Lord, have mercy" (12) and the prayer "Most Holy Trinity," the holy doors are opened

> **Priest**: "Wisdom."

> **Choir**: "More honorable than the Cherubim."

> **Priest**: "Glory to Thee, O Christ God."

> **Choir**: "Glory, Both now,"

"Lord, have mercy" (3), "Bless." The Priest makes the dismissal with the commemoration of the holy temple and the holy day. After this the holy doors are closed again.

4. The Priest accompanied by the Deacon makes three small bows before the holy table and recites only: "O God, be merciful to me a sinner." They kiss, as was already noted, the Holy Gospel, the holy table and the altar cross. Then the Deacon, having received permission from the Priest, goes out through the northern doors and, having stood at the usual place, makes three small bows, saying nothing and says: "Bless, Master." The Priest, standing before the holy table and making with the Holy Gospel the sign of the cross over it, exclaims: "Blessed is the kingdom."

> **Choir**: "Amen."

Immediately the

> **Reader**: "Come, let us worship"

(3) and reads the opening psalm (see nos. 102, 118, 119, note).

5. The Deacon returns into the sanctuary through the southern doors, and the Priest, having stood before the holy doors, reads the Vespers (Lamp-lighting) Prayers from the fourth to the eighth, for the first three he will read later, at the Antiphons

6. At the end of the opening psalm the Priest returns through the southern doors into the sanctuary, and the Deacon, having gone out through the northern and stood at the usual place, sings the Great Litany. After the exclamation, having made a small bow, he returns through the southern doors into the sanctuary. The Reader begins the 18th Kathisma of the Psalter. At "Alleluia" – they make small bows. When at each of the following Antiphons "Glory" is said, the Deacon goes out through the northern doors from the sanctuary and at the designated place sings the Small Litany, and the Priest recites quietly the first, second and third Vespers Prayers. After the completion of the Small Litany the Deacon returns through the southern doors into the sanctuary, and the Priest says the exclamation, as prescribed

7. At the beginning of the reading of the psalms [stichologia], if the Presanctified Lamb is kept in the tabernacle (artophorion) of the holy table, the transfer to the table of oblation takes place thus:[^785] the Deacon brings to the holy table the holy diskos, the star-cover and the small veil. The Priest kisses the Holy Gospel and places it on the right side of the holy table. After this he places the diskos on the unfolded antimension [iliton], on its left side, and, having opened the tabernacle, makes a small bow. He takes the chalice with the lid, in which the Lamb is kept, places it on the middle of the antimension [iliton] and, having taken from it the Presanctified Bread, places it with great piety on the holy diskos, as also the particles needed for the communion of the faithful. Having placed the pyx back into the tabernacle, he closes it and, having placed the holy diskos on the middle of the antimension [iliton], censes the star-cover and the small veil and covers the diskos with it. Having taken the censer, he censes around the holy table, preceded by the Deacon with a lighted candle. Having returned before the holy table and given the censer to the Deacon, he makes a low (prostrate) bow, making the sign of the cross on himself, after which he takes with both hands the covered holy diskos and, holding it on his head crosses by the right side of the holy table to the table of oblation (altar of preparation), preceded by the Deacon with a lighted candle and censer

8. At the table of oblation the Priest places the diskos on the unfolded antimension [iliton], after which he pours wine and water into the chalice, as is the custom, saying nothing at this. After censing the veil of the chalice over the censer he covers the chalice with it. Then with the large veil, which he likewise censes, he covers the diskos and chalice, saying nothing at this, but only: "Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us." Having made a prostrate bow, the Priest and deacon return to the holy table. There the Priest places the Book of the Holy Gospels on the folded antimension [iliton]

9. If the Presanctified Lamb is kept in the tabernacle which is located on the table of oblation, then at the beginning of the reading of the psalms [stichologia] the Priest and deacon go to the table of oblation. Both make a small bow before it, the Priest opens the tabernacle and, having made again a small bow, censes with three swings the Presanctified Gifts. Then he takes the Presanctified Bread from the pyx and places it with great piety on the diskos, and pours into the holy chalice, according to custom, wine and water, saying nothing. He takes the censer, censes the star-cover and veils, covers the diskos and chalice, each – with its own veil and both – with the large veil (aer), saying nothing, but only: "Through the prayers of the holy fathers." Having made a prostrate bow, he returns to the holy table

10. If the Priest deems it appropriate, he finishes the rite of placing the Lamb on the diskos during the reading of the first Antiphon, the censing – during the second, and the transfer of the Presanctified Gifts – during the reading of the third Antiphon

11. If a larger number of faithful is expected for communion, so that the Presanctified Bread alone will not suffice, the Priest places the appropriate number of already consecrated particles on the diskos, and on top of them – the Lamb Itself

12. After the completion of the reading of the psalms [stichologia] the Choir begins the psalm "Lord, I have cried," and the Deacon censes according to the prescription (see no. 33), at this he censes the Presanctified Gifts – three times, each time – with three swings

13. During the singing of "Glory, Both now" the holy doors are opened and the Entrance takes place in the usual manner. The Deacon censes, if there be an Entrance with the Gospel, and makes the Entrance with the Gospel

14. When the Deacon says in a low voice: "Let us pray to the Lord," the Priest recites quietly the Prayer of the Entrance with its exclamation and, after the completion of the stichera, the Deacon exclaims: "Wisdom, arise."

> **Choir**: "O Gladsome Light."

They enter the sanctuary, then the Deacon, turned to the holy doors, says: "Let us be attentive." The Priest, having turned to the people, blesses: "Peace be to all."

> **Deacon**: "Wisdom, let us be attentive."

The Choir sings the Prokimenon of the first Paremia.

> **Deacon**: "Wisdom."

Reader, having stood in the middle between the two choirs and looking to the east: "The reading from the Book of Genesis."

> **Deacon**: "Let us be attentive."

The Reader reads the first Paremia. After this the Choir sings the second Prokimenon.

15. Immediately after the second Prokimenon the Deacon says to the

> **Priest**: "Command,"

and the Priest takes with both hands the lighted candle and simultaneously the censer, stands before the holy table, looking to the east and, making the sign of the cross, exclaims: "Wisdom, arise." After this he turns to the west, towards the people, makes again the sign of the cross and says in a raised voice: "The Light of Christ illumines all." At these words all Who are in the sanctuary and in the church make three great prostrations. The Priest turns again to the east and gives the candle and censer to the server.

> **Reader**: "The reading from the Book of Proverbs."

> **Deacon**: "Let us be attentive."

The holy doors are closed and the second Paremia is read.

16. After the completion of the second Paremia the Priest says to the

> **Reader**: "Peace be to Thee,"

and the

> **Deacon**: "Wisdom, let us be attentive."

After this the Deacon, having taken a lighted candle, approaches the Priest.

The Reader, who stands in the middle between the two choirs, or rather the Priest, who stands in the sanctuary before the holy table and censes, sings: "Let my prayer be set forth."

After the singing of this verse by the Reader or priest, the Choir sings it once more.

Then again the Reader or priest, who now, accompanied by the Deacon going in front, stands on the southern side of the holy table and censes there, sings the first verse of the 140th Psalm: "Lord, I have cried," and the Choir repeats: "Let my prayer be set forth."

And again the Reader or priest, accompanied by the Deacon, stands at the east of the holy table, censes there and sings the second verse of the psalm: "Set, O Lord, a watch before my mouth," and the Choir sings: "Let my prayer be set forth."

After this the Reader or priest, preceded by the Deacon, stands on the northern side of the holy table, censes there and sings the third verse of the psalm: "Incline not my heart," and the Choir sings: "Let my prayer be set forth."

And once more the Reader or priest accompanied by the Deacon, again stands before the throne, censes there and sings: "Let my prayer be set forth as incense before Thee," and the Choir finishes: "the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice."

17. It should be noted that during the singing by the Reader or priest of "Let my prayer be set forth" or the verse, the Priest censes the holy table with three swings at the beginning and at the end of each verse which he sings. At this time the Choir and the faithful pray on their knees. When the Choir sings the Priest, having given the censer to the server, and all who are in the sanctuary, pray likewise on their knees. After the completion all bow three times

18. If on these days of Lent falls the memory of a certain saint or a temple feast, having opened the holy doors, the Deacon exclaims: "Let us be attentive," and the Reader reads the Prokimenon of the Apostle, after which the Apostle and Gospel are read, as prescribed

19. The holy doors are closed and the Deacon, having received permission from the Priest, goes out through the northern doors and, having stood at the designated place, sings the litany "Let us all say." Everything else takes place according to the prescription until the very exclamation of the prayer for the catechumens, after which the Priest, having laid aside the Gospel, unfolds the antimension [iliton] on the holy table

20. From Wednesday of the fourth week of Great Lent, which is the midpoint of the Forty Days, after the exclamation "That with us they also," the Deacon dismisses the catechumens, and having invited to prayer those preparing for holy baptism: "All catechumens, depart. Catechumens, depart. All who are for illumination, approach" and so it is sung at all services of the Presanctified, even if a feast day fell, with the exception of Saturday and Sunday

After this follow the prayers of the faithful, according to the prescription.

21. After the exclamation "According to the gift of Thy Christ"

> **Choir**: "Amen"

and sings the hymn "Now the Powers of Heaven." The Deacon, having returned through the northern doors into the sanctuary, opens the holy doors and, having taken the censer, censes with three swings only the front of the throne, then – the table of oblation and the Priest. Then he stands before the throne to the right of the Priest and holds the censer on the ring finger of his left hand. The Priest and deacon, with hands raised up, recite together "Now the Powers of Heaven" three times, each time making a small bow.

22. Then they go directly to the table of oblation. There the Priest, having taken the censer, censes with three swings the Presanctified Gifts, saying nothing at this, takes the large veil (aer) and places it on the left shoulder of the Deacon, then takes the covered holy diskos with his right hand and holds it on his head, and the chalice with wine – with his left hand at his chest

23. If, however, the diskos should not have a foot, the Priest places it on the covered chalice, which he holds with his left hand, and with his right hand holds the veil over the holy diskos and carries the chalice like a diskos to his forehead

24. They go out of the sanctuary through the northern doors, in front walks the Deacon, who frequently censes the Holy Gifts. During the procession no one says anything. When they enter through the holy doors into the sanctuary, the Priest places the holy diskos on the throne on the left, and the holy chalice – on the right side, removes the small veils from the diskos and chalice and places them on the holy table, and with the aer, which he takes from the shoulder of the Deacon and censes over the censer, covers the Holy Gifts, saying nothing, but only censing the Holy Gifts thrice. After the completion of the hymn "Now the Powers of Heaven" all make three great prostrations, after which the holy doors are closed and the curtain is drawn shut

25. The Deacon, having bowed to the Priest, goes out through the northern doors and, having stood at the usual place, exclaims: "Let us complete," "Help us, save us, have mercy." The Priest exclaims: "And vouchsafe us, O Master," and the people: "Our Father." The Deacon girds himself with the orarion crosswise, as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom

26. According to the prescription follows the bowing of heads, and after the prayer "Look down, O Lord Jesus Christ" the Priest and deacon make three small bows, after which the Priest does not undercover the Holy Gifts, but, placing his right hand under the aer, touches the Life-giving Bread piously and with fear, and at the words of the Deacon "Let us be attentive" exclaims: "The Presanctified Holy Things to the holy."

Then the Priest removes the aer and, having folded it, places it aside, as also the star-cover. The Deacon enters through the southern doors into the sanctuary, stands to the right of the Priest and, having made a small bow, says: "Break, Master, the Holy Bread," and the Priest breaks it and places the four parts on the diskos just as it takes place at the Liturgy of Chrysostom, and the particle with the inscription "IC" he places into the holy chalice, saying nothing. The Deacon pours a little warm water into the chalice, if there exists a custom, saying nothing and stands somewhat to the side. The Choir sings the Communion Hymn "Taste and see," and also a second one, if the Apostle and Gospel of some saint or temple saint were read.

27. The Priest and deacon communicate according to custom of the Holy Bread. Then the Priest wipes his fingers with a sponge, if there is a custom to use it, and, having kissed it, places it on its place

The Deacon wipes the holy chalice, saying nothing and, having made three small bows, after the curtain of the iconostasis has been drawn open, opens the holy doors. Having received the chalice from the Priest, he approaches the holy doors and, lifting it, shows it to the people, saying: "Draw near."

> **Choir**: "I will bless the Lord at all times. Alleluia."

The communion of the faithful takes place just as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom, and the Priest, giving the Holy Bread, says the words of this Liturgy "The precious and most holy." The transfer of the holy diskos takes place just as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom.

The Priest makes a small bow, takes the holy chalice, turns to the holy doors, looking at the people, says quietly: "Blessed is God," and then exclaims: "Always, now and ever."

28. Everything else takes place just as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom. However, it should be noted that: 1) at the dismissal of this Liturgy the author is not mentioned; 2) in the three first days of Passion Week one must say the dismissal of Palm Sunday at Vespers: "Christ, our true God, Who came to His voluntary Passion."

After the completion of the Liturgy of Presanctified Gifts the Priest and deacon take off the holy vestments, saying nothing.

### In Concelebration of Two Deacons

1. After the completion of the Hours and after the dismissal at the end of the Typika the holy doors are closed, the Priest and deacons make before the holy table three small bows each, saying: "O God, be merciful to me a sinner" and kiss the Holy Gospel, the edge of the holy table and the altar cross, as usual. After this the 1st deacon, having paid respect to the Priest, goes out through the northern doors and, having stood at his place before the holy doors, makes three small bows, saying nothing, after which he exclaims: "Bless, Master."

> **Priest**: "Blessed is the kingdom."

> **Choir**: "Amen"

and the Reader reads the opening psalm. The Priest, having gone out through the northern doors, reads the Vespers Prayers, from the fourth to the eighth.

At the end of the opening psalm the 1st deacon goes out through the northern doors and sings the Great Litany. After the exclamation "For to Thee belongs" the Deacon returns into the sanctuary.

2. The first deacon assists the Priest during the placing of the Presanctified Lamb on the diskos and its transfer to the table of oblation, and the 2nd deacon goes out through the northern doors and sings the first Small Litany. The 1st deacon sings – the second and finally the 2nd deacon – the third

3. The censing on the psalm *“Lord, I have cried”* and the entrance take place just as at Vespers in concelebration with two deacons (see no. 39). Having returned into the sanctuary, the 1st Deacon exclaims from the holy doors: "Let us be attentive." The Priest, turned to the people: "Peace be to all."

> **Second Deacon**: "Wisdom, let us be attentive."

The Choir sings the Prokimenon of the first Paremia.

> **First Deacon**: "Wisdom."

> **Reader**: "The reading from the Book of Genesis."

> **Second Deacon**: "Let us be attentive."

The Reader reads the first Paremia, after which the Choir sings the second Prokimenon. After the second Prokimenon the 1st deacon, turning to the Priest, says: "Command." The Priest takes the candle and censer and makes the sign of the holy cross, as was said above.

> **Reader**: "The reading from the Book of Proverbs."

> **Second Deacon**: "Let us be attentive."

4. After the second reading of the Old Testament both deacons go before the Priest when he censes the holy table and sings: "Let my prayer be set forth" with the verses of the 140th Psalm

5. If the memory of some saint or a temple feast falls, the 2nd Deacon exclaims: "Let us be attentive." After the Prokimenon of the Apostle the

> **First Deacon**: "Wisdom."

After the reading by the Reader of the title of the Apostle the

> **Second Deacon**: "Let us be attentive."

After the completion of the reading of the Apostle the Priest says: "Peace be to Thee."

> **First Deacon**: "Wisdom, let us be attentive."

Choir sings "Alleluia".

The censing before the Gospel takes place just as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom in concelebration of two deacons (see no. 155). Then the

> **First Deacon**: "Bless, Master, the proclaimer."

> **Priest**: "May God, through the prayers"

and gives Him the Gospel.

> **Second Deacon**: "Wisdom, arise, let us hear the Holy Gospel."

> **Priest**: "Peace be to all."

1st deacon, having stood on the ambo or somewhat before the holy doors: "The reading from the Holy Gospel according to (Name)."

> **Second Deacon**: "Let us be attentive"

and everything else, as is customary.

6. After the reading of the Gospel the deacons, having gone out through their doors, stand at the designated places. 1st deacon begins: "Let us all say." Then

> **Second Deacon**: "Pray, ye catechumens."

> **First Deacon**: "All catechumens."

> **Second Deacon**: "Catechumens, depart"

and again

> **First Deacon**: "Only the faithful."

From the Wednesday of the fourth week of Lent they sing thus, as is given further.

> **First Deacon**: "All catechumens."

> **Second Deacon**: "Catechumens, depart."

Again

> **First Deacon**: "All who are for illumination, approach. Pray, ye who are for illumination."

> **Choir**: "Lord, have mercy,"

and the

> **First Deacon**: "Ye faithful, for the brethren who are preparing for holy illumination."

Priest – exclamation: "For Thou Art our enlightenment."

> **First Deacon**: "All who are for illumination, depart."

Again

> **First Deacon**: "Only the faithful."

Then

> **First Deacon**: "Help us, save us, have mercy,"

"Wisdom."

> **Second Deacon**: "Again and again,"

"Help us, save us, have mercy," "Wisdom." The deacons enter through their doors into the sanctuary.

7. During the singing of the hymn "Now the Powers of Heaven" the holy doors are opened and the deacons, having taken censers, cense with three swings (thrice) only the front of the holy table, then – the table of oblation and the Priest. After this they stand to the right and left of the Priest, holding the censers on one of the fingers of the left hand, and recite with the Priest three times the hymn "Now the Powers of Heaven."

Then they go straight to the table of oblation. There the Priest censes the Presanctified [Gifts] and, having taken the aer, places it on the left shoulder of the 1st deacon, and all go out in the usual manner. In front go both deacons and frequently cense the Holy Gifts.

8. After the holy diskos and the holy chalice are placed on the holy table, the deacons go out through their doors and stand at the usual places. 1st Deacon exclaims: "Let us complete." At "Our Father" the deacons gird themselves with the oraria crosswise

> **Second Deacon**: "Bow our heads unto the Lord."

After three small bows the 1st Deacon exclaims "Let us be attentive" and after the exclamation of the Priest "The Presanctified Holy Things to the holy" both deacons return through their doors into the sanctuary.

> **First Deacon**: "Break, Master, the Holy Bread."

The deacons communicate of the Holy Bread, according to custom. After the communion of the Priest and deacons, the 1st deacon wipes the holy diskos over the holy chalice and calls: "Draw near."

The rest takes place just as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom.

### Without a Deacon

1. If this Liturgy is celebrated without a Deacon, the Priest exclaims everything that belongs to the Deacon, as has already been said in the rubric of Vespers and the Divine Liturgy of John Chrysostom

2. When the Priest censes the holy table and transfers the Holy Gifts to the table of oblation, the server, holding a lighted candle, walks before him. Small litanies and exclamations the Priest says, if possible, before the holy table

3. During the singing of "Let my prayer be set forth" the server walks with a lighted candle before the Priest

4. At the Great Entrance candle-bearers, if there be such, turned to the northern doors and arranged in order, accompany the Presanctified Lamb. After they arrive before the holy doors they stand together on both sides, and then return to their places

### In Concelebration of Priests

1. The rules of concelebration of the Liturgy of Presanctified Gifts – are the same as of Vespers and the Liturgy of Chrysostom. Only one must keep in mind that:

- At the end of the Typika concelebrants vest in sacred vestments, saying when putting on each only: "Let us pray to the Lord."

- The principal celebrant exclaims: "For to Thee belongs," "For a merciful," "According to the gift of Thy Christ," "For Thou Art our sanctification." Other exclamations are exclaimed by concelebrants in turn.

- At "Let my prayer be set forth" concelebrants remain in their places, stepping back slightly from the holy table when the principal celebrant needs to pass, together with the principal [celebrant] they bend their knees and rise.

## A

### Ancient Liturgical Gospels (Ostroh, Vatican)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Readings & Scriptures*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 93, L102*

[93] The most important readings, without doubt, -- are the Sunday and Saturday ones, since in the most ancient Gospels readings are given only for these two days of the week, so in the Ostroh one and in two Vatican ones: one Greek of the 9th century and one Slavonic Glagolitic of the 11th century.

---

## B

### Biblical Odes (Odes of Holy Scripture)
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Part 1 Structure, L174*

Although now we do not use the Odes of Holy Scripture presented at the end of the Psalter, excluding the Forty Days, nevertheless, we leave something from them, that is at the 8th Ode, instead of Glory – the refrain 'Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord,' and the refrain to the Katavasia of the 8th Ode: 'We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord, praising and magnifying Him unto all ages,' which is sung according to the tone of the Katavasia; also the Song of the Theotokos 'My soul magnifies' before the Heirmos of the 9th Ode of the canon, which we take also in the time of the Forty Days, and outside of it, with the exception of Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos, on which, according to ancient typikons, it is not proper to take [it].

---

### Biblical Odes in the *Triodion* Canon
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Part 4 *Triodion*, L211*

6. Odes and Canons. The Biblical Odes, given at the end of the Psalter, are intertwined with the odes of the canon, as given: before the ode of the canon the corresponding ode of the Psalter is recited, leaving its last verses for refrains to the troparia of the canon, in such quantity as there will be troparia in the ode of the canon, including the heirmos, except two, for to the penultimate troparion we refrain "Glory", and to the last – "Both now". The 2nd Ode is recited in full before the ode of the canon, and to the troparia of its canon we refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee". According to our ancient custom, the Odes of the Psalter are recited only in those odes in which the triodion occurs, and in the other odes we refrain the usual refrains to the troparia of the canon. The Greek Typikon prescribes singing the Odes of the Psalter in the tone of the *Menaion* canon, but now we do not even know what their melody was.

---

### Blessing of Water on August 1
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 454, L475*

[454] Although Greek typikons do not give the blessing of water on this day, however, this custom, inherent to Greek-Slavs, is taken from the Greeks, who once had the custom of performing the blessing of water at the beginning of each month and, accordingly, on 1 August, according to the testimony of Balsamon in the explanation of Canon V of the Trullan Synod: Haec statuente canone, novilunium quidem festum ante annos omnem memoriam supeantes cessavit; eius loco, Dei gratia, ut et ipse propitious reddatur, preces, as Aquae lustrales in Ecclesia a populo fideli fiunt in uniuscuiusque mensis principio (Asseman. Calend. Tom. I. Cap. XI. Pag. 156) /Establishing this canon, truly the new moon feast, which from ancient times erased all memory of it; in its place, thanks be to God, and better prayers take place, and sanctification of water in the church, which the faithful people perform at the beginning of each month (Assemani, Calend., Vol. III, Part I, Chapter XI, p. 156)/.

---

## C

### Canon for the Dead and Panikhida
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 107, L117*

[107] Slavonic typikons, in order not to discard the canon for the dead, transfer it to the Panikhida over the Kolyva, or to Compline (Pochaiv *Octoechos* at the end and Moscow Typikon, chapter 12). The Greek Typikon in chapter 6, instead of the Martyria canon, prescribes the canon for the dead; however, with such a decision the Martyria canon would never be taken: neither on these Saturdays, nor on Souls Saturdays, for even on these Saturdays that same Typikon does not prescribe the Martyria canon. Probably ordinary Octoechoi did not have it.

---

### Canon Structure (Litanies, Hymns, Sessional Hymns, Kontakia, Exaposteilaria)
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Part 1 Structure, L176*

After the 3rd, 6th and 9th Ode of the canon, immediately after the Katavasia, the Small Litany is taken (according to the model given at the first Kathisma of Matins), each with its own exclamation, and after the litany at the 3rd Ode the Sessional Hymn is sung, at the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos, and at the 9th – the Exaposteilarion (Hymn of Light) is read. Both the Kontakion and Ikos are taken once each, the Sessional Hymn on Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos – twice, that is once – simply the Sessional Hymn, and the second time – with the refrain Glory, Both now. And the Exaposteilarion on Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos is taken three times, that is twice – simply, and the third time – with the refrain Glory, Both now. On the Feast of a Polyeleos or non-Polyeleos Saint, which is celebrated, according to the Slavonic Typikon, on 6, the Sessional Hymn and his Exaposteilarion are taken twice , then Both now: his Theotokion. If the Saint has two Sessional Hymns or Exaposteilaria, then they are taken once each, that is the first – simply, the second – with the refrain Glory, then Both now: his Theotokion . When several services coincide, each with its own Sessional Hymn, Kontakion-Ikos and Exaposteilarion, then they are taken one after another, according to the order of services; however, the Kontakion-Ikos of the first service is taken at the 6th Ode in its place, and the Kontakion-Ikos of the second, according to the Slavonic typikons , is transferred to the 3rd Ode and goes immediately before the Sessional Hymn. The sequence of Sessional Hymns and Exaposteilaria in the middle of a Feast of the Lord and of the Theotokos ends with the Sessional Hymn or Exaposteilarion of the Feast. After the Katavasia of the 9th Ode, according to the Slavonic Typikon, 'It is truly meet' is taken, if it is not Sunday. If it is Sunday, 'It is truly meet' is not taken, but then, between the Small Litany and the Exaposteilarion (Exapostolarion) we sing, according to the tone of the Prokeimenon of the Liturgy, the troparion 'Holy is the Lord our God' (3)" .


> [!NOTE]
> **Royal Doors 2026 Current Usage Note:** In the 2026 propers, the traditional Greek term **Exaposteilarion** is overwhelmingly replaced with the descriptive translation **Hymn of Light** (occurring 44 times vs. only 6 times for Exapostilarion). Furthermore, the canonical term **Heirmos** (or **Heirmoi**) is never used; instead, Royal Doors exclusively uses the phonetic Slavonic spelling **Heirmos** (561 times) or **Katavasia** (395 times) to designate these canon hymns. Sessional hymns are referred to as **Sessional Hymn** (191 times) or **Kathisma Reading** (136 times).

---

### Censing at the Litiya (Lytia)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 14, L15*

^[14] Since no Typikon (the Synod testifies) prescribes censing in the temple here, it would be better if the deacons cense from the place of the Litiya when they arrive there. And since this is better, we have placed such a rubric in the text, and we have completely rejected the worse existing local custom of censing the Holy Table and the local icons as at "Lord, I have cried," although the Synod mentions it too. However, if there are icons in the narthex, it is proper to cense them first, for the ancient Typikons prescribe so.

---

### Compline and Midnight Office on Feasts without Vigil
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 341, L362*

[341] Since ancient typikons do not give All-Night Vigil, nothing is mentioned about the troparia at the blessing of loaves; but to sing: troparion to the saint once, Glory, Both now: to the feast, as the Pochaiv *Anthologion* has, does not correspond to the rite, according to which troparia are taken at the All-Night Vigil. -- "If there is no All-Night Vigil, at Compline -- Kontakion to the Saint, Glory, Both now: of the Feast". At Midnight Office, after the 1st Trisagion -- Troparion of the Feast; after the 2nd -- Kontakion of the Feast; we do not say the prayer "Remember", but "Lord, have mercy" (12) and dismissal. Thus in Slavic menaia.

## D

### Daily Vespers (without Kathisma)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Part 1 Structure, L92*

This Vespers is celebrated just as Daily [Vespers] , however, without a Kathisma and without litanies, except for the last 'Have mercy on us, O God,' which only the Slavonic Typikons present, but the Greek do not prescribe. The stichera at 'Lord, I have cried' will be only 4. The dismissal, although it can begin from 'Glory to Thee, O Christ God,' yet with us is exclaimed also before that: 'Wisdom!' and 'More honorable' just as at Daily Vespers.

---

### Dismissals (Feast vs. Day Commemorations)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 317, L337*

[317] The ancient Lviv *Horologion* gives the dismissal of the feast, however, since in all other cases dismissals of feasts begin with Vespers of the feast, rightly the *Tserkovne Oko* and Pochaiv *Menaion* give "dismissal of the day", with commemoration, as it seems to us, also of the saint who falls on this day.

---

### Dogmatikon and Afterfeasts on Fridays
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 376, L397*

[376] Thus in chapter 43 of Mark, *Tserkovne Oko*, Pochaiv *Menaion* and Moscow Typikon; however, if there is to be uniformity in typikons, then we think that here too the 1st Theotokion of the tone should be according to the general rule of the Afterfeast of the Lord and the Theotokos, given at the end of the Pochaiv and Moscow *Octoechos* under the prescription about the temple of the Resurrection of Christ; and if -- not, then also in the Afterfeast of other feasts there should be a stichera of the Feast, which would be in greater conformity with ancient typikons, in which neither on the Forefeast, nor on the Afterfeast, nor on the Apodosis of the Feast is the Dogmatikon given on Friday evening, but only stichera of the Feast, regardless -- whether it is Saturday or another day of the week. (Our handwritten Typikon, chapter 20 and chapter 11 of Mark in the *Tserkovne Oko*), although general Slavic typikons on the Fore- and Afterfeast and on the Apodosis of the Feast give the Dogmatikon. Moscow Typikon 12 September, 24 March, 14 August; *Tserkovne Oko* 12 September, 21 September; Pochaiv *Menaion* 12 September; Typikon of the Lviv University, p. 87.

- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 184, L201*

[184] So unanimously all Slavonic typikons.

## E

### Exaltation of the Holy Cross (Flowers and Basil)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 259, L278*

[259] More simply, according to the ancient rule, the cross with basil is placed on a tray. Today's Greeks more often, instead of basil, place flowers under the cross.

---

### Exaposteilaria, Kontakia, and Theotokia after Canons
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 127, L139*

[127] Moscow Typikon, chapter 4, and Peremyshl, page 85. -- Mark in chapters 78 and 79 prescribes after the 3rd Ode the Sessional Hymn of the saint, Glory, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone, that is Sunday, after the 6th -- Kontakion of the saint. New Constantinopolitan Typikon after the 3rd Ode: Κοντακιον το αναστασιμον χύμα, είτα ψαλλεται το Κάθισμα του Αγιου, και το θεοτοκιον; μετά δε την εκτην ωδην Κοντακιον και Οίκος του εορταζομενου Αγιου /Kontakion of the resurrection spoken, then is sung the Kathisma of the saint, and the Theotokion; after the 6th Ode Kontakion and Ikos of the celebrated Saint/. Greek Typikon in chapter 2, after the 3rd Ode -- Κάθισμα του Μηναίου /Kathisma of the *Menaion*/, after the 6th -- Κοντακιον του Αγιου /Kontakion of the Saint/, after the 9th -- Εξαποστιλαριον το αναστασιμον και του Αγιου ει εορτάζεται, και το θεοτοκιον /Exaposteilarion of the resurrection and of the Saint if he is celebrated, and the Theotokion/, but does not indicate, which Theotokion; however, Slavonic typikons rightly prescribe the Theotokion of the Sunday Exaposteilarion, for it corresponds to the Sunday Gospel.

## F

### Feast of St. Catherine (Transfer of Feasts)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Monastic & Parish Celebrations*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 279, L298*

[279] We find the Service of St. Catherine as having Polyeleos only in our Pochaiv *Menaion* and in the new Greek-Venetian one; but in others -- without Polyeleos. In later Greek typikons we find it given on 25 November with the Apodosis of the Feast of the Entry into the Temple of the Most Holy Theotokos, and in earlier ones -- on the 24th, as it is today among Greek-Slavs. Thus the Greek-Venetian *Menaion* of 1615 gives: Σημειωσαι ουν, ότι ευρομεν εν τισι Τυπικοις των νεωτέρων, ότι εν τιοα των πόλεων ψαλλεται η ακολουθία της αγίας μάρτυρος Αικατερίνης εν τη κε του μηνός, εν η και αποδιδοται η εορτή. Εν ετεροις δε Τυπικοις παλαιοτεροις ευρομεν αυτήν εορτάζεσαι εν τη κδ του αυτού μηνός: εν δε τη κε ψαλλομεν την ακολουθίαν του εν αγιοις Κλημεντος Παπα Ρώμης, και Πέτρου Αλεξανδρείας, εν η και αποδιδοται η εορτή των Εισοδιων /Note, therefore, that we found in some newer typikons, that in some places the service of the holy martyr Catherine is sung on the 25th day of this month, on which the feast is also given up. In other older typikons we found that her memory is celebrated on the 24th of this month, and on the 25th we sing the service of Saints Clement Pope of Rome and Peter of Alexandria, and on this day also the feast of the Entry is given up/. This transfer from the 24th to the 25th day, in the opinion of the Greeks, as explained by the new Greek-Venetian *Menaion* (24 November, p. 158), was done at the wish of the monks of Mount Sinai, so that it would not coincide with the Apodosis of the feast and, so that in this way the memory of the saint would be honored more solemnly. For we know that the body of the holy great martyr was transferred by angelic power to Mount Sinai and buried there.

[193] General Slavonic typikons give the Heirmos only on Annunciation and on the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos; but our Service Books and the new Greek Constantinopolitan Typikon -- on all feasts of the Theotokos and of the Lord, until the Leavetaking.

### Feasts of Saints (Service of St. Anne)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Monastic & Parish Celebrations*
- **Source Reference:** *Part 3 *Menaion*, L2387*

Although even in ancient typikons the Service of St. Anne is given of small type with the service of the *Octoechos* and of the holy women , however, with time it was honored with us with Polyeleos, and by the decision and decree of the Synod of Zamość, even with All-Night Vigil  (although with us there is none, but only Polyeleos); and with the Greeks – Great Vespers with stichera at the Litya, and also Great Matins, from the canon and further .

### Feasts of Saints (St. Peter and Paul stichera)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Monastic & Parish Celebrations*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 282, L301*

[282] The ancient handwritten *Menaion* that we have gives the stichera of the Praises only to Peter; and the handwritten typikon -- stichera of the Praises to Peter, and afterwards -- the Aposticha of the feast.

### Feasts of the Holy Apostles (Vigil and Polyeleos)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Monastic & Parish Celebrations*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 704, L725*

[704] With the exception of the Chiefs of the Apostles Peter and Paul on June 29 and the Beloved Apostle on September 26 and May 8, to whom the rubrics prescribe a Vigil, to other Apostles and Evangelists ancient rubrics prescribe a service only on 6, without Doxology; but in our and Russian rubrics Polyeleos is prescribed to them.

### Forefeast and Afterfeast Rubrics
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 171, L187*

[171] Μαρκ. Καιφ. οε /Mark, chapter 75/, having given this typikon for the Afterfeast, adds: Ωσαύτως γίνεται και εις τα Προεορτια /Likewise it happens also in the Forefeast/. Pochaiv *Anthologion* November 20. In the most ancient Menaia two saints in the Forefeast never have two separate troparia.

## G

### Gospel at Lazarus Saturday Matins
- **Category:** *Liturgical Readings & Scriptures*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 570, L591*

^[570] Neither our Manuscript Typikon, nor the Typikon of the Lviv University, nor *Tserkovne Oko*, nor the Pochaiv *Triodion* of 1767, nor the Ostromir Gospel prescribe here the Gospel at Matins. Two most ancient Vatican codices prescribe it... also the Greek Typikon of Sabbas, of the new ones -- Pochaiv *Triodion* 1786, Greek Bologna *Triodion* 1724, new Constantinopolitan Typikon and new Athenian *Triodion*.

## H

### Holy Doors vs. Royal Doors (Historical Usage & Rubrics)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Objects & Architecture*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 264, L283*

[264] Ancient Greek typikons mention nothing about a deacon, neither at the bringing out, nor at the exaltation, nor at the laying of the precious Cross, but only about one priest. The Greek typikon, similarly to the Slavic ones, prescribes for the priest to vest in all priestly vestments: αλασσει ο Ιερεύς πασαν την ιερατικην στολην /the priest vests in all priestly vestments/. The Greek *Triodion* (Sunday of the Veneration of the Cross) and the new Constantinopolitan Typikon, similarly to Slavic typikons, prescribes for the priest to enter with the cross from the sanctuary to the temple through the northern doors: εκ του αριστερού Βήματος /from the left side of the sanctuary/. Greek typikons, with the exception of the new Constantinopolitan, and the Slavic of the Lviv University, prescribe for the priest, having exited from the sanctuary to the temple, to head to the entrance doors that lead from the temple to the narthex, which are sometimes called royal, and there await the end of the Doxology and from there exclaim "Wisdom, attend", and then head to the tetrapod, which is before the iconostasis. Although these doors are called royal, βασιλικαι /royal/, one must understand that they were called so in the past. Today we call royal the middle doors of the iconostasis, which according to ancient custom are called holy: αγιαι ΰυραι /holy doors/ (chapter 96, Greek Typikon).

### Holy Doors vs. Royal Doors (Terminology)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Objects & Architecture*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote [754], Appendix, L66*

[754] Ed. note. In ancient times, "Royal Doors" referred to those doors that led from the narthex to the temple, for at them the Patriarch met the Emperor. Later this name was applied with improper meaning to the middle doors of the iconostasis. In the rubrics of modern Greek liturgical books, "holy doors" are given (see Akolouthia tou Esperinou kai tou Orthrou, Roma 1950, p. 16), therefore we also consistently correct "Royal Doors" to "Holy Doors" everywhere in this Typikon.

### Holy Liturgy (Concelebration & Repetition)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Monastic & Parish Celebrations*
- **Source Reference:** *Point 97, Appendix, L275*

97. According to the ancient custom of the Eastern Church, only one Holy Liturgy may be celebrated at the same holy table. However, one may depart from this rule if the Divine Liturgy must be repeated for the benefit of the faithful. If there is one or several secondary churches in the parish, then the more solemn Liturgy is celebrated in the main sanctuary, and other liturgies should be celebrated rather in the side sanctuaries.

### Hymn 'Holy is the Lord our God' and its Verses
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 38, L41*

Regarding the troparion "Holy is the Lord our God," neither the ancient Greek Typikons nor the Euchologia prescribe to take it three times, nor do they adduce its verses. However, the Slavonic rubrics and the new Constantinopolitan Typikon prescribe to take it three times; regarding the verses -- they do not agree. Our Service Book and the new Constantinopolitan Typikon present only one verse; ours: "Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship at His footstool, for He is holy" (5th verse of the 98th psalm, from the last verse of which this troparion is taken). Constantinopolitan: Υψουτε Κυριον τον θεον ημών /Exalt ye the Lord our God/. The Tserkovne Oko and following it the Moscow Typikons present two verses, namely: 1. "For holy is the Lord our God"; 2. "Over all people is our God." In our opinion, if the troparion must be taken three times, then one verse is not sufficient; therefore it is possible to divide the verse "Exalt ye" into two parts, of which the second would begin from: "And worship at His footstool" etc.

## K

### Kathisma 'Blessed is the Man' on Feasts
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 277, L296*

[277] Some consider, according to the edition of the Peremyshl Typikon of 1870, p. 271, that neither on St. Michael, nor on St. Prophet Elias, should *“Blessed is the man”* be sung and, that then not a single kathisma is taken, for this kathisma, as the publisher writes about it, is found only in the Pochaiv *Anthologion*, and in the most ancient menaia and Anthologia they are not mentioned; the reason for this is considered to be that "Elias did not die, and St. Michael, as bodiless, is not subject to death". However, this is not enough. For regarding the rule, not only the Pochaiv *Anthologion* (*Anthologion*) of 1777 and the Pochaiv *Menaion* of the same year, but also the Lviv *Anthologion* (*Anthologion*) of 1643 and the Great Typikon, under the title *Tserkovne Oko*, printed in Moscow in 1615, that is more than a century and a half before the Pochaiv *Anthologion*, and the manuscript *Anthologion* of 1736, which we have, and the Typikon of the All-Russian Church, printed in Moscow in 1859, by the decision of its Governing Synod, give also on these two feasts the kathisma *“Blessed is the man”*. Although some rules, like the Moscow *Menaion* of 1782, the Greek-Venetian of 1884 do not give *“Blessed is the man”*, it does not follow from this that no kathisma is needed, for even on Saints without Polyeleos in the *Menaion* a kathisma is not given, but the sequential one is meant; so here one can understand the sequential one, which three ancient handwritten Slavic typikons give: one -- of the Lviv University, the second -- of St. Onuphrius in Lviv, and the third -- of the library of the Chapter of St. George; also *Tserkovne Oko* (which gives two rules: one with *“Blessed is the man”*, and the second with the sequential kathisma). The reason that these rules give for these two feasts a sequential kathisma, may lie in the fact that their service initially had neither All-Night Vigil nor Polyeleos, but gradually, with time, grew into All-Night Vigil. About St. Elias it is written in the Pochaiv *Menaion*: "Let it be known that in printed Greek menaia, in handwritten typikons, and also in Slavic handwritten and printed typikons, the service of the Prophet Elias is given on 6, with *Octoechos*". And regarding St. Michael, the above-mentioned Slavic typikons give him a service only of the Polyeleos type, but incomplete, for they partially combine his service with the service of the *Octoechos*, as for a Saint without Polyeleos.

### Kathismata and Small Litanies at Matins
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 77, L86*

[77] When two kathismata should be read, and when three, we noted in the note to the Order of Daily Matins on page 41. Regarding small litanies which are read between kathismata and sessional hymns, the Lviv Synod, our Horologions and our Service Books (at the end) give them also at Small Matins, and they are used also by the Greek-Melkites (according to the testimony of their patriarch bl. m. Clement Bahous). Conversely, in the Russian Typikon, approved by their Governing Synod (Moscow edition of 1859), in the Order of Daily Matins it is written that the priest says them only at the Vigil and when the memory of saints having a Polyeleos and Doxology is celebrated; similarly also in the new Wallachian-Bucharest Typikon, in which in the Order of Daily Matins is given: "We take sessional hymns from the *Octoechos* without litanies" (untranslatable); and adds: "In monasteries, usually, between kathismata litanies are taken only on Sunday and when more special saints occur". From the Greek Typikon no conclusion can be made, for in it small litanies are not mentioned neither at Small Matins, nor at Great, nor before the Canon, nor after the Canon. It is assumed in the Typikon that this is known to everyone. From the rubrics of the Greek *Triodion*, given at Matins on Meatfare Saturday, one can conclude that these litanies should be said also at Small Matins. For it gives: η συνηιϊης στιχολογια. Εν δε ταις συναπταις πασαις της στιχολογιας και του Κανόνος, μνημονεύονται πάντες οι προαπελΰοντες Πατέρες και αδελφοί ημων /Ordinary Stichology. In all small litanies of the Stichology and of the Canon, all our fathers and brethren who have passed away before us are commemorated/. Let everyone observe the rubric and custom of his Church. Finally, in our opinion, later typikons reject litanies here only for the sake of greater shortening of the divine service; if the single difference between Small and Great Matins were the rejection or use of litanies, then this difference should have been indicated in some place of ancient liturgical books; however, this is not encountered. What the exclamation of the third litany should be is not indicated in any of the church books. Therefore we are forced to borrow it from Great Matins. At Great Matins in Slavonic books two exclamations are given which are used at the third litany, that is one -- for Sunday "For blessed is" and the second -- for Polyeleos feasts "For holy Art Thou". For the sake of distinguishing the Sunday day from the ordinary day, at Small Matins it is appropriate to use the second "For holy Art Thou", although it would not be bad to use also the first "For blessed is" (Οτι ευλογητοα), for in Greek books we find only this one exclamation, without distinction of day. Regarding Sessional Hymns, they are taken two or three after each stichology, depending on the edition, except the Theotokion. In Lviv editions of the *Octoechos* and in the Greek-Venetian one, only to the Theotokion is sung "Glory, Both now". In the Pochaiv and Moscow ones a separate refrain is also given to every second, or even to the third sessional hymn. This refrain, corresponding to the content of the sessional hymn: on Monday and Tuesday -- Penitential "O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger"; on Wednesday and Friday -- of the Cross, and on Thursday -- of the Apostles; to the third sessional hymn, that is the Martyron -- also the Martyron refrain: "Wondrous is God in His saints".

### Liturgical Readings (Prokeimena, Alleluias, Apostle-Gospel, Communion Hymns)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Readings & Scriptures*
- **Source Reference:** *Part 2 General Rubrics, L123*

7. If there be several Prokeimena, Alleluias, Apostle-Gospels and Communion Hymns, then one must know how to take them. Know first, that in church typikons more than two are not given, with the exception of Apostle-Gospels, of which only in Slavonic typikons three are given, for the Slavs are richer in supplications than the Greeks. For where three readings coincide, the Greek typikons do not give the sequential one, but the Slavonic ones take it under the refrain of the first reading, as if one with it . When this is impossible, on the occasion of some great feast, then they order to take it on the day before under the refrain with the sequential one . However, this rule has been preserved among us perhaps only in cathedral churches, for in others usually only one Apostle-Gospel is taken, as also one service either of the day, or of the saint, or one for need. If, therefore, there be two Prokeimena and two Alleluias, then both are taken under one heading, that is both Prokeimena – before the refrain of the first reading, both Alleluias – after the completion of the second reading. However, the first Prokeimenon is taken twice, namely: once – before and once – after the verse, the second – only once and without a verse, for in this case the Typikon does not give a verse. Similarly also "Alleluia": both of its verses are taken only of the first service, and of the second – only one first verse . The Heading, that is from whom: from Paul, from Matthew or from another, is taken only of the first reading, and the others usually are not taken, although it would be better to announce the headings of other readings as well, for it is not indifferent to the listeners to know the reading of which holy author is being proclaimed; and for this reason only would the rubric make certain sense, which orders to take the sequential reading under the refrain, for taking one reading under the refrain of another means merging it with the previous one because its heading is not announced. If the heading of the following third reading, which is not taken under the refrain, is not named, then it should have been said that this third reading is also taken under the refrain. "Let us be attentive" is announced only at the beginning of the first reading. If there be two Communion Hymns, then "Alleluia" is repeated only upon the completion of the second .


> [!NOTE]
> **Royal Doors 2026 Current Usage Note:** In 2026, Royal Doors shows full compliance with Dolnytsky terminology for readings: **Prokeimenon** is used exclusively (333 times) instead of "Prokimenon," and **Communion Hymn** is the standard title (126 times), with "Communion Verse" occurring only 3 times.

## P

### Paschal Procession and Reception of Light
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 615, L636*

^[615] According to the ancient rubric of community life the procession goes from the temple into the narthex through the northern doors of this narthex and there, before its central doors leading into the temple, the beginning of Matins is sung. Carried are: Gospel -- by the priest and censer -- by the deacon, preceded by candle-bearers, brethren with lit candles, as you have in the Greek *Pentecostarion*. To this the Pochaiv *Triodion* adds the icon of the Resurrection of Christ, and *Tserkovne Oko* -- also the icon of the Most Holy Theotokos and other holy icons, carried by priests and deacons, so that in such a way the procession would be more majestic, than only with candles. According to the custom of the surroundings of Greece, independent of the Patriarch of Constantinople, before this procession the bishop or priest, standing in the holy doors with a lit candlestick in hand, exclaims in a loud voice: "Come ye, take light from the unwaning light, and glorify Christ, who is risen from the dead", that is "Come, receive light from the unwaning light and kiss Christ, risen from the dead". And so all approach one by one, to light their candles from him, forming after this the procession (The Holy Passions. Athens. 1892)

## S

### Saints 'on 4' and Alleluia Services
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 45, L49*

[45] According to the ancient rubric, a saint "on 4" could be of two types: that is, either with a troparion or without a troparion; and when the saint has no troparion, then at Matins, instead of "God is the Lord," "Alleluia" was sung and the divine service had a separate rubric. But in our current Horologia, troparia are given for every day of the month, and therefore at Matins we always sing "God is the Lord," and we limit the "Alleluia" service to Great Lent, as do the Greeks.

### Shroud (Epitaphios) Placement and Custom
- **Category:** *Liturgical Objects & Architecture*
- **Source Reference:** *Part 4 *Triodion*, L729*

Regarding the time and place of the placing of the Shroud we do not find an ancient rubric, for this rite is later and different in different regions. According to the custom of our archcathedral church the Shroud remains hung behind the holy table, over the High Place, from Resurrection Matins to the Leavetaking of the Resurrection inclusive, that is until Wednesday before the Ascension. According to the custom of our other churches, the Shroud, taken from the Tomb before Resurrection Matins, is placed on the holy table, where it remains during the whole Bright Week, and from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas to the Leavetaking of the Resurrection – behind the holy table. According to others – it remains on the altar, the antimension with the Gospel is placed on it and the Liturgy is celebrated on it. However, it is better to place the Shroud behind the holy table, for lying on the altar, it is often significantly damaged by candles, from which wax drips on it.

### Singing of 'Christ is Risen' from Pascha to Ascension
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 626, L647*

^[626] So about "Christ is risen" in our Service Books, except "We have seen", and in its place they have "Christ is risen", however, such is our custom and so in the Pochaiv *Triodion* of 1786... and in the Moscow Typikon of 1859... Ancient Greek rubrics prescribe "Christ is risen" only instead of "Blessed be the name" and instead of the psalm "I will bless the Lord", as in the Slavonic Typikon of the Lviv University. A later custom of the Greeks -- to sing "Christ is risen" after "Blessed is the Kingdom" three times and, instead of "We have seen the true light" and instead of "Blessed be the name of the Lord", -- three times. However, some of them, after "Blessed is the Kingdom" sing "Christ is risen" with its verses, as is given at the beginning of Resurrection Matins. The Moscow Typikon follows them, but the new Constantinopolitan Typikon does not go. What we said about the custom of the Greeks, we took from a description which we have from the island of Corfu, in which is written the following: "After 'Blessed is the kingdom' the priest 'Christ is risen', and successively repeat it, first the right followed by the left choir; and this happens on all the days of Pascha until the Ascension. But on the great Sunday, and on those of the New Week we follow to sing it after its verses unchanged; as was said previously at Matins... Is sung successively 'Christ is risen' – as much on the great Sunday as on the remaining days of Pascha at 'With fear' instead of 'We have seen the light', and before the Dismissal three times flowingly instead of 'Blessed be the name', and at the end, at the Dismissal instead of 'Through the prayers' /After 'Blessed is the Kingdom' the priest: 'Christ is risen', successively again repeat it: first -- the right, then -- and the left choir. And so it will be on all days from the Resurrection to the Ascension. But on the Great Sunday and on the days of Bright Week we continue to sing invariable this with its verses, as is taken at Matins ... Successively is sung 'Christ is risen' on the Great Sunday as much as on the rest of the days of the Resurrection: at 'With fear', instead of 'We have seen the light' and before the dismissal three times flowingly, instead of 'Blessed be the name' and at the end, at the dismissal, instead of 'Through the prayers of our holy fathers'/.

### Trisagion in Afterfeast and Bright Week
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 201, L219*

[201] According to the most general and most ancient typikons in the Afterfeast and on the Leavetaking the Trisagion should be taken, and not "As many as have been baptized into Christ" or "Before Thy Cross", for they are taken on the very day of the feast, with the exception of "As many as have been baptized into Christ", which is taken not only on the very day of the Resurrection, but also throughout the whole Bright Week, since throughout the whole Bright Week the divine service takes place as on the very day of the Resurrection. On other days, until the Leavetaking of the Resurrection, the Trisagion is taken. So have the general Greek and Slavonic typikons and the most ancient Typikon of the Monastery of St. Nicholas of Casole in the district of Otranto, kept in the Barberini library in Rome, written six hundred or seven hundred years ago. In it on fol. 121 and 124 is given the Typikon, which I gave. With this general and ancient typikon one Greek Typikon does not agree, written by the Reverend Father Bartholomew, a companion of the Reverend Father Nilus and co-founder of the Monastery of Grottaferrata near Rome, kept in that same monastery, which prescribes "As many as have been baptized into Christ" until the Leavetaking of the feast. E.g. December 26 gives: Και αντί του Τρισάγιου Οσοι εις Χριστον. Τούτο γαρ λεγομεν έως ου αποδιδοται η εορτή /And instead of the Trisagion As many as have been baptized into Christ. For this we say until the feast is taken leave of/. Does not agree also the new Constantinopolitan Typikon 1851, marked with the seal of the patriarch. See, e.g. on Monday of the Holy Spirit there, where Greek and Slavonic *Triodia* have the Trisagion, this Typikon has "As many as have been baptized into Christ". Regarding Troparia, Mark thus: Sunday, Glory: Troparion to the saint, if he has, Both now: Kontakion of the feast (Καιφ. ξε)/chapter 65/.

### Trisagion vs. 'As Many as Have Been Baptized into Christ'
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 183, L199*

[183] 2 Ancient Greek Typikon of the Monastery of St. Nicholas των Κασουλων /of Casole/ (Ed. Note: a place in Puglia, southern Italy, where the Monastery of St. Nicholas was located) in the village of Otranto (Bibliotheca Barberina) prescribes "As many as have been baptized into Christ" also on the Transfiguration. And the Greek Typikon of Grottaferrata, that is of the monastery of the reverend father Nilus, near Rome, gives "As many as have been baptized into Christ" not only on the very day of the feast or in Bright Week, but also on all days of the Afterfeast until the Leavetaking of the feast; similarly also the new Constantinopolitan Typikon; however, the Greek Typikon, called of St. Sabbas, and following it also Slavonic typikons do not agree with that, for on Thomas Sunday and on Monday after the Descent of the Holy Spirit they explicitly prescribe the Trisagion. Does not agree also the Typikon, called of St. Nicholas.

### Troparia and Kontakia of the Saints
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Part 1 Structure, L214*

3. In older Menaia, which our Menaia also follow, troparia and kontakia are not given to every Saint, but in closer times we find them given in our Horologia. Therefore one should not wonder if regarding the use of troparia at the Hours the rubrics in some way do not agree with the *Menaion* and our Horo- or Prayer Book. For when a Saint had a troparion and kontakion, according to the ancient Typikon, they were taken at all Hours; but according to the Typikon of our Horo- and Prayer Books, in order not to repeat at all Hours on all days one and the same troparion and kontakion, for a certain variety at the 1st Hour – the troparion and kontakion of the day of the week, at the 3rd and 9th – of the Saint, and at the 6th – of the Temple.

---

### Troparia of the Day, Temple, and Saints
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 20, L21*

^[20] However, it is better presented in the Greek Horologia -- only one troparion, that is of the current Saint, or the four aforementioned: "O God of our Fathers" with the three others, without distinction of day. In the Greek Menaia the Saint does not always have a troparion and, when he does not have one, then the general troparia are taken -- "O God of our Fathers"; when he has one, then to the Saint. With us, because the current Saint in the *Menaion* always has a troparion, then, if it were taken always, the troparia "O God of our Fathers" would be superfluous; so that they not be superfluous, they are taken daily, and to the Saints -- only to the Polyeleos ones. The troparion of the day and of the Temple is given only in the Slavonic Typikons.

### Troparion and Kontakion of Forefeast and Saints
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 180, L196*

[180] According to the previous typikon: troparion of the Forefeast and to the saint, if he has, Glory: Kontakion to the saint, if he has, Both now: Kontakion of the Forefeast; everything else -- only to the saint, and Apostle-Gospel also of the day, in the first place. Also to the second saint is taken, if he has something. Before the troparia of the saint Slavonic typikons prescribe to the temple of the saint (Pochaiv *Triodion*, fol. 11, on the verso.).

### Troparion of the Saints at Hours
- **Category:** *Hymnographic Elements & Structures*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 285, L304*

[285] According to the ancient rule the troparion of the saints is taken with Glory, also on the 1st and 6th hours; but with us today -- only the one of the day.

- **Category:** *History & Rite Identification*

### Typikons
- **Category:** *History & Rite Identification*
- **Source Reference:** *Intro, L215*

Ritual unity is achieved through the observance of unified rubrical prescriptions. From ancient times, the Eastern Churches began to use collections of such prescriptions, that is, Typikons (from the Greek word typikon).

---

## V

### Vespers and Vigil on the Eves of Nativity and Theophany
- **Category:** *Liturgical Services & Offices*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 318, L338*

[318] According to our most general and Russian typikons, Vespers with the Service of Basil on the Eve of the Nativity of Christ begins at the seventh hour of the day (At one in the afternoon), and on the Eve of Theophany -- at the fifth hour of the day (at eleven before noon, according to the present calculation); but according to other most ancient typikons in both cases: περί ωραν δεκατην της ημέρας/around the tenth hour of the day/ (at four in the afternoon). All-Night Vigil according to the general Slavic [typikon], among which also *Tserkovne Oko* -- at the tenth hour of the night (that is in the morning); according to others, the most ancient, on the Eve of the Nativity: περί ωραν πρωτην της νυκτός /around the first hour of the night/, and Theophany: περί ωραν δεύτερον της νυκτός /around the second hour of the night/. In the Constantinopolitan Patriarchate Vespers begins immediately after the ninth Royal Hour.

## W

### Weekday Commemorations (Moscow Typikon)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Monastic & Parish Celebrations*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 334, L354*

[334] The Moscow Typikon adds also the sequential (it is meant, if there is no dispensation); according to the ancient rule it would be necessary to add also to the saint, if he has something, however, for a saint without Polyeleos with us usually nothing is taken.

### Weekday Liturgy Commemorations (Greek vs. Slavonic)
- **Category:** *Liturgical Monastic & Parish Celebrations*
- **Source Reference:** *Footnote 91, L100*

[91] The Greek Typikon gives the whole service only to the saint, and Apostle and Gospel -- first of the day, and then of the saint; Προκειμενον του κατά την ημεραν Αγιου, Αλληλούια του Αγιου, Ευαγγελιον της ημέρας και του Αγιου. (Καιφ. σ) /Prokeimenon of the saint of the day, Alleluia of the saint, Gospel of the day and of the saint (chapter 6)/. So also in chapter 99, Mark. Although this rubric is given only in the Saturday service, however, it must be understood that also on other days of the week it should be so. Slavonic typikons prescribe the whole service to the day and to the saint, if he has one, and troparia -- also to the temple, if it is of the Lord or of the Theotokos. The Moscow Typikon also prescribes to the temple, if the temple is of a saint (although this does not agree with the rubric of that same Typikon, given on September 26 and January 30); this same Typikon ends the Kontakia with the Kontakion for the Dead *“With the saints give rest”* with the refrain "Glory" and the Kontakion of the temple, if it is of the Lord or of the Theotokos, if -- not, then with the usual "Protection" ("O Undisputed Intercessor") with the refrain "Both now" (chapter 52). This custom we find also among Greek-Italians and Greek-Melkites, but it does not exist among Constantinopolitan Greeks and Athonites, with the exception of some. But, since according to the rubric of the Greek Typikon, two Apostles and two Gospels were to be taken, and according to the Slavonic rubric, also the whole service of the day and of the saint, if he has one, and, since many saints (over one hundred eighty) have an Apostle and Gospel, as follows from the content of the Apostle-Gospel, therefore, in order to shorten the duration of the divine service, followers of the Greek Rite began already many years ago to reject certain rubrics; therefore also our Ruthenians take at the Liturgy only the service of the day, and reject the saint without Polyeleos; some -- conversely: take only the service to the saint, and reject the service of the day, as evidenced by the Pochaiv Service Book of 1765, which gives the Apostle and Gospel only on Sundays, and on weekdays -- only in Bright Week and in the week after the Descent of the Holy Spirit, similarly as Latin Missals, which give the Apostle and Gospel of the day only in these two mentioned weeks, for Great Lent and for certain other days. This custom we find also among Greek-Italians, observed also by some of those who are called Orthodox, whom the Moscow Typikon accuses, saying: "The Ecumenical Church does not take neither on the Beatitudes, nor at Liturgies the Apostle and Gospel to the saint on every day, only the sequential, that is the pillar throughout the whole year, in sequence, as also of selected saints who have an Apostle and Gospel. And if the Apostle and Gospel of the saint is read every day, then this is from one's own ignorance, and not according to the church typikon" (chapter 58, at the end). Exactly so also in the manuscript of the three-hundred-year-old Gospel that is among us. However, this rubric of the Ecumenical Church is not observed by the Constantinopolitan Hierarch, called Ecumenical, nor by the Churches subject to him, who (according to the testimony of hierarch Benjamin Νεαπολεος /of Neapolis/, who lived in Constantinople and on Mount Athos, who in our times accepted church union) have the custom, also in monasteries, to take the Apostle and Gospel only of the day, if the saint does not have one, if he has, then only to the saint, and in another they adhere to the new Constantinopolitan Typikon, printed in the patriarchal typography in 1851, marked with the patriarchal seal and confirmed by signatures of all patriarchs and hierarchs subject to them. In this Typikon there, where the rubric gives two Apostles and Gospels, one Apostle-Gospel is given, that is the Apostle -- of the first service, and the Gospel -- of the second service. Thus e.g. October 26, November 21, when they fall on a Sunday and on John the Theologian May 8, when it falls on Ascension.

But in our current Horologia, troparia are given for every day of the month, and therefore at Matins we always sing "God is the Lord," and we limit the "Alleluia" service to Great Lent, as do the Greeks. When the Kontakion is only for one saint, then it alone is taken at all [hours]; and when for neither, nor for the feast, then the Hypakoe of the tone is taken; for general Greek editions do not have Sunday Kontakia. Regarding the Hypakoe, you have the rubric in Greek Horologions at the 1st Hour, it and at the other hours must be observed.
[^66]: Lviv Synod in heading 5. According to the Typikon given at the end of our Apostles, and in our previous ones, as also in some Greek sluzhebnyky in Goar, the daily antiphons "It is good" are given, also on Sundays, with the refrain only Sunday on the 3rd antiphon, as the Italo-Greeks also observe. General Greek sluzhebnyky give the Typika on Sunday, and Octoechoi also on weekdays; for in them are given daily stichera on the "Beatitudes", by which is understood the presence of the Typika. With such a difference of typikons let everyone preserve the custom of his Church, and among us the Typikon is -- of the Synod. In vain during the Synod some tried, saying, that to take daily antiphons, instead of the Typika, does not correspond to our rite; for daily antiphons are given not only by the aforementioned sluzhebnyky and apostles, but also by Greek Readers [Anagnostiki] and the Moscow Typikon in chapter 25, and St. Sophronius himself, Patriarch of Jerusalem, in the 7th century, in the explanation of the Divine Liturgy (Spicileg. Rom. tom. 4, nn. 12, 13, 14. Propag. 1840) -- mentions nothing about the Typika, but only about the antiphons "It is good". About the Typika we assume that they were left for the case when there is no Liturgy. For in the beginning numerous in monasticism were of the laity, who could not serve the Holy Liturgy; and therefore, instead of the Liturgy, they had to use the Order of Typika; therefore also the Synod limits them to days in which there is no Liturgy, so that in this way the memory of them was preserved only in monasteries. It is equally good to use antiphons, as also the Typika, when it is taken fully; but when from every psalm only one verse is taken and without stichera on the "Beatitudes", as they practice, then it is better to use antiphons. Finally, the full Typika is quite long and in present times was shortened.

Καιφ. ξη. and on verso. /Mark, chapters 68 and 79/; as also our *Menaion* September 7, if it falls on a Sunday). In previous typikons the saint sometimes did not have a troparion, and sometimes also a Kontakion; sometimes he had either only a troparion, or only a Kontakion, sometimes also a Prokimenon-Alleluia and Apostle and Gospel, and Communion Hymn. However, because later among us troparia and Kontakia were added to all saints, that in the sequence of the Menology, services to a saint without Polyeleos at the Liturgy are not taken; the Greeks, in the case of a saint who has an Apostle-Gospel on a Sunday began taking the Apostle only to the saint, and the Gospel -- only of the Sunday.
